Just Announced! On Oct 8, the authors of “Against Tech Oligarchy” bring together labor leaders and tech critics to pack the jury in the trial of a tech billionaire.

Witnesses will present Bezos’ most notable injuries to the working class and together we’ll decide his fate. Join us for an event that is sure to be a boisterous, cathartic celebration of working class solidarity and power.

Against Tech Oligarchy: Worker Resistance in the World’s Most Powerful Industry

The Trial of Jeff Bezos is part of the Against Tech Oligarchy book tour. As tech bosses fall in line with the right, tech workers have begun fighting back. This is the rousing inside story of their movement—and the way it spawned an anti-worker backlash now reshaping the industry. The authors will be attending the event and signing books.

Get tickets at KeysComedyClub.com and experience The BS Show—a Toronto comedy bucket show inspired by the stand-up-and-interview format of Kill Tony! Every Wednesday at Keys Comedy Club, comedians take a chance on the bucket for an unpredictable night of live stand-up comedy, spontaneous conversations, and big laughs.

Here’s how it works: sign up, put your name in the bucket, and wait to see if you’re selected. When your name gets pulled, you get THREE MINUTES onstage to deliver your jokes. Whether you’re an experienced Toronto stand-up comedian or trying comedy for the first time, those three minutes are your chance to show the room what you’ve got!

After your set, stick around for an interview with host Brian Couto and the special guest panel. Your jokes are only the beginning—the conversation afterward brings out your personality, unexpected stories, and moments nobody could have planned. Come ready to perform, answer questions, and enjoy the fun.

With a new special guest panel weekly, The BS Show brings fresh personalities and reactions to every edition. If you enjoy Kill Tony-style bucket shows, comedy open mics, crowd interaction, and discovering new comedians, this Toronto comedy night gives you plenty to watch—and the chance to participate yourself.

Join us every Wednesday at Keys Comedy Club, located at 844 Bloor Street West, lower level, Toronto. Performer sign-up starts at 8:00 PM, and the show begins at 8:30 PM. Bring your best three minutes or bring your friends and watch the bucket decide who takes the microphone next!

Looking for things to do in Toronto on a Wednesday night? Make it a night of live comedy at The BS Show, hosted by Brian Couto. Three-minute sets, interviews, a weekly guest panel, and a bucket full of possibilities—reserve your spot at KeysComedyClub.com and come see whose name gets called!

🎤 Get tickets from KeysComedyClub.com before they sell out! Join us tomorrow, Thursday, October 8 at 8 PM, for a Toronto stand-up comedy open mic and Pro/Am night at Keys Comedy Club, 844 Bloor St. W. Bring your friends and make your Thursday night a comedy night!

Looking for things to do in Toronto tomorrow? Experience live stand-up comedy on Bloor Street, where comedians take the stage to share fresh material, sharpen their punchlines, and bring their personalities to the microphone. If you love discovering local talent, a Toronto comedy open mic is a fun way to experience the city’s comedy scene.

Your host is KeyEpic, an Armenian-Lebanese Toronto stand-up comedian and owner of Keys Comedy Club. With a passion for spreading laughter, KeyEpic brings his humour and stage presence to a night that celebrates comedians putting in the work, developing their voices, and connecting with a live audience.

The October 8 lineup features Amar Batzorig, Andrés Cervantes, Sharan Jaideep, Alexander Brovedani, Dan Weston, Jeff Hobbs, Sean Creighton, Chris Armstrong, MucGlow-Gun, Ryan Francis, Jason, and Robby Frankel. Join Host KeyEpic for a Pro/Am comedy night featuring different perspectives, styles, and plenty of fresh jokes.

Whether you’re planning a Toronto date night, a night out with friends, or a solo adventure, Keys Comedy Club offers a chance to enjoy live entertainment and support local stand-up comedians. TOKiMONSTA and Vjollça at Standard Time! 

GRAMMY-nominated producer TOKiMONSTA (Jennifer Lee) has charted a fascinating career over the past 10+ years. She is one of the most revered music producers as one of the pioneers of the seminal 2010 era “L.A. Beat Scene.” Known for her genre-blending sound and innovative production, her seventh album, Eternal Reverie, explores themes of resilience and joy, capturing the transformative power of music. After overcoming personal challenges, including a life-threatening brain condition, she continues to push creative boundaries, blending influences from global cultures. With a career marked by fearless experimentation, TOKiMONSTA remains a dynamic force in electronic music, inspiring and transporting listeners. 

Join us on a Thursday evening as Vjollça starts things off at 9pm.

Looking forward to welcoming TWO SHELL + Nautiluss and Phialefti this Friday presented by Standard Time x Not Dead Yet! 

Two Shell are British electronic music’s great enigmas - a duo who built their reputation on concealment, wit, and refusing to play by the industry’s rules. For years, the conversation centered on mystery, but that’s beginning to shift. The duo are now in the midst of a personal and creative shift, moving toward a renewed sense of presence and openness. 

Where they once kept themselves entirely guarded, Two Shell have started to loosen their grip on the mythology, appearing publicly as themselves and engaging more directly with fans. Beneath the games and misdirection, their core belief remains simple - that music, at its best, doesn’t need to be solved, only felt. 

Kicking off the night, local underground stalwart Nautiluss (aka HEADRUSHH), whose track “Wifi Oasis” featured on the first-ever Two Shell DJ Mix (ɪᴍᴘᴀᴄᴛ21, 2020), will warm up the room with a voyage straight through the veins of the Hardcore Continuum. Expect everything from Bleep and UK Hardcore to Jungle, UKG, Grime, UK Funky, Bassline and Dubstep, alongside a cameo from Phialefti, a rising Toronto talent he’s been crafting music with for the past 15 months.

Ivkovic is someone who applies a curatorial mindset and a deep love of music to all of his creative exploits. Yes, he’s a DJ, but he’s so much more than that; he’s a storyteller, a connoisseur and, most importantly, an artist.

Ma Sha is a New York-based producer, DJ, and label head whose electrifying take on experimental club music has become a vital force in the global underground. Since co-founding the event series Kindergarten in 2017, she has cultivated a distinct sonic universe that bridges raw rhythm with dancefloor dynamism. Rooted in the transatlantic techno continuum, her sound channels high-voltage energy through warped percussive forms and bass-heavy textures. Drawing from her experience as one half of the duo Sha Ru and her upbringing within a vibrant DIY scene, Ma Sha’s work reflects a deep commitment to sonic exploration and community building. As the founder of Kindergarten Records, she curates forward-facing club releases that blur genre lines and invite kinetic engagement. Her productions, featured on labels like Steel City Dance Discs, Nervous Horizon, and TraTraTrax, are known for their ricocheting rhythms and metallic impact”

Ben UFO - Open to Close at Mooi! 
Presented by Standard Time x Paradox 

Ben UFO: (Open to Close - Room 1)

747 b2b Emily Nicoll (Room 2)
Caleb Klager (Live - Room 2)

This event will also be hosting the Black Sunflowers TIFF premiere afterparty

No photos / video

Room 1: Over the past five years, Ben UFO has acquired a deserved reputation as one of contemporary dance music’s most daring and wide-ranging selectors, with his keen ear and razor-sharp technical abilities enabling him to cut between eras, lineages and mixing styles with dazzling ease and fluidity.

It’s refreshingly difficult to pin down what makes Ben’s DJing distinctive and exciting, whether you encounter it on the radio, in a recorded mix or on the dancefloor. If there’s a core characteristic of his approach it’s an infectious warmth and restless love of exploration, exemplified by his habit of meshing mind-bendingly strange tracks into peak-time sets, and by the way his Thursday night shows on Rinse FM weave together jacking unreleased dance cuts with new finds and dubbed-out oddities from across the globe. In the club, he shapes these elements into something rich and unpredictable, interspersing phases of driving momentum with joyful curveballs and ruptures in the flow that jolt you back to your senses — moments, as he describes it, that feel like coming up for air on the dancefloor.

Room 2: Paradox curates a lineup of Toronto’s staple underground artists. The kind of names that mean everything to those who’ve been paying attention.

747 and Emily Nicoll open the night for a extended b2b . Co-founders of the highly regarded Aquaregia label, and with 747’s sets having resonated across some of the world’s most celebrated clubs and institutions, this is an opening that demands your attention from the first record.

Closing out the night, Caleb Klager takes the floor for a live hardware set. An artist spoken about in hushed tones by those who know. Consistently pushing the boundaries of sound and leaving the room inspired.

TEED is a US-based, UK-born artist, producer, singer-songwriter, DJ, classically trained musician, label head, and two-time GRAMMY-nominee. Standard Time welcomes KiNK (live) alongside anise b2b noa! 

KiNK has become one of house music’s most in demand producers and remixers: his tracks easily stand out in any club night and they are second to none in the most competitive environment electronic music has ever seen. His abilities in finding the ‘sweet spot’ of new machines and even of sounds considered ‘classic’ and to reshape them into totally different beasts would be totally enough to justify the phenomenon.

KiNK’s live sets hold the key to understanding how he creates unparalleled enthusiasm on stage and through his studio output. KiNK’s live sets simply take the hood off – strictly in terms of sound. A small set up of machines and controllers is all there is, but every knob turned produces an audible result. Often he will pass a machine to the audience and incorporate their input in real time. This happens at mind-boggling speed. Hyperactive, yet holding down grooves to kill for. KiNK’s ability to nail smash beats on the fly, well visibly and audibly, that most people couldn’t program in weeks of studio work – this ‘credibility of sound’ right where it matters is what sparks the love everywhere he visits.

noa approaches DJing as composition, using tracks as tools to build layered, dynamic pieces of music that evolve into a narrative of sound across dancefloors in real time. noa’s sets are alive, purposeful, and in constant conversation with the room. Standard Time welcomes back Jacques Greene alongside Leevisa and DJ EEEEEE! 

Jacques Greene has been making music about the club for over a decade. Across multiple EPs, singles, and two acclaimed full-length albums, Feel Infinite (2017) and Dawn Chorus (2019) his sound has evolved into an emotional, atmospheric haze that balances intimacy with physicality. In 2020, he released ANTH01, a collection of unearthed early works and previously unreleased tracks that traced the foundations of his musical language. 

Alongside his solo work, Greene is one half of Verses GT, a fully realized collaboration with Nosaj Thing that exists as the group, the album, the live show, and the visual world surrounding it. Built through in-person sessions across London, Los Angeles, Tokyo, Paris, and Montreal, Verses GT is a heavyweight, intentional body of work rooted in human connection, shared headspace, and distilled emotion, featuring contributions from George Riley, Kučka, and TYSON. 

Greene also hosts a monthly residency on Rinse FM, now running for over three years, where he explores deep club music, new material, and long-form mood-driven selections. Beyond his own releases, he has collaborated with Bonobo, remixed Radiohead, produced for Jessy Lanza, arlo parks, Tinashe, and toured internationally with The xx, continually refining a sound that is both deeply personal and built for collective experience. 

Working across ambient composition and electronic music, Leevisa brings an approach shaped by the simplicity of lived experience and emotion. Named by i-D Magazine as one of Seoul’s rising female artists, she has performed at venues and festivals including Halle am Berghain (DE) and Unsound. Let’s celebrate Tiga’s new album release on June 5th as Tiga, Tony Price and Guthrie join us at Standard Time! 

Tiga, born in Montreal, is a globally renowned DJ, producer, and the creative force behind Turbo Recordings. His journey began in the vibrant chaos of the 1980s Indian club scene, where he developed a deep appreciation for electronic music’s transformative power. Returning to Montreal in the early 1990s, Tiga pioneered a new wave of nightlife, introducing innovative party concepts, guest DJs, and Montreal’s first rave, “Solstice,” in 1993. His relentless pursuit of musical excellence saw him co-founding the legendary nightclub Sona, creating a sanctuary for bold, cutting-edge dance music, while his label Turbo Recordings became a launchpad for numerous iconic releases in electronic music from legends such as Chromeo, Azari & III, Gesaffelstein, Duke Dumont, ANNA, and Charlotte de Witte. 

As a producer, Tiga achieved global recognition with his chart-topping cover of “Sunglasses at Night,” a collaboration with Zyntherius, which became an anthem for electro enthusiasts. His remix credits include high-profile artists such as The xx, LCD Soundsystem, Moby, Depeche Mode, and Justice, solidifying his reputation as a master of reinvention. Tiga’s contribution to the prestigious DJ Kicks series showcased his eclectic style, while his original works, including the hit single “Pleasure from the Bass,” cemented his place in the pantheon of electronic music. At we kick on in 2026, Tiga’s new album HOTLIFE serves as his latest statement, featuring the likes of Fcukers, Boys Noize, Maara, and MRD alongside production credits from Paranoid London, Jump Source, and Matthew Dear. 

With his infectious creativity and a career spanning decades, Tiga continues to captivate audiences worldwide, shaping the sound of modern club culture.

Tony Price will also be playing live and Guthrie from Turbo, Montreal will be on opening duties.

The body of work that Chilean-born interdisciplinary artist Matias Aguayo has made over the years defies conventional classification. Thanks to his idiosyncratic approach, it has allowed him to forge a unique artistic path, leaving a distinctive and indelible mark in every discipline he explores.

Throughout his career, Aguayo has fused electronic music, performance, theater, art, composition, and community outreach into a fun-yet-profound singular vision that continue to expand. Each project bears his unmistakable brand of humor and avant-garde spirit.

Social outreach has remained a constant in Aguayo’s artistic life. His work spans homeless shelters, retirement homes, prison outreach, and hospitals like the Pitié-Salpêtrière. Projects like BumBumBox and Nueva Red De Bailadores reclaim dance as a political and communal act in public spaces, merging his artistic vision with a broader commitment to social change.

Kenny Glasgow is a North American electronic music pioneer, a role he’s held for over two decades.Though the Canadian star has spent the last 5 years as the half of the acclaimed duo Art Department, functioning as a musical engineer, composer of both music and lyrics, and vocalist, he is now returning to his solo roots. 

Nitin’s story begins with Detroit, the techno mecca that has spawned an endless lineage of talent over the last 30 years. The sounds that emanated from Motor City through his radio in London, Ontario left an indelible imprint and inspired him to embark on a career that continues to flourish to this very day. Record shopping in Detroit led to a meeting with Mike Huckaby and Nitin subsequently playing the legendary Shelter at the age of 17. From there on in his fate was sealed.

One war. More than 300 letters. One remarkable Toronto love story. 🇨🇦 

The St. Andrew’s Society of Toronto is proud to present The November Project at Rivoli on Wednesday, October 7.

Horgie served overseas with various units including the 48th Highlanders of Canada. His young wife Peachie remained at home in Parkdale, Toronto.

Through the UK, Italy, Belgium, Holland and Germany, he kept writing home.

More than 300 letters survived — capturing the love, humour, fear and uncertainty experienced by a Toronto couple separated by the Second World War.

Their grandson, Rob Horgan, later transformed those letters into The November Project, bringing his grandparents’ story to the stage through readings from their original correspondence.

Rob is joined by Eve Goldberg and a ukulele ensemble performing songs from the WWII era.

Last year’s performance sold out Rivoli.

🎟️ Only 100 tickets are available for this year’s performance.

📍 Rivoli — 332 Queen St. W.

🎭 A milestone night in the Back Room! 🍳✨

We are thrilled to present “Cook Your Life”, a Cantonese one-person theatre comedy written and performed by HKAPA-trained stage actress, director, and Artistic Director of Heart Theatre — May May Chan (陳慧心)!

This special evening marks the very first Cantonese theatre comedy on stage in The Back Room at Rivoli! 🎉

🍲 About the Show: Cook Your Life

Life throws all kinds of flavors at us—sweet, sour, bitter, and spicy. But just like cooking, the outcome is always in your control. You decide what ingredients to bring to the table, how much seasoning to add, and how to handle the heat.

Through witty humor, relatable life stories, and cooking as an analogy for life’s everyday challenges, May May takes us on a hilarious yet heartwarming journey on how to master your own recipe for life.

300+ letters. One war. A Toronto love story. ❤️ 

The November Project tells the extraordinary story of letters that kept a Toronto couple connected during the Second World War. This moving musical theatre production was inspired by the wartime correspondence between creator Rob Horgan’s grandparents, “Horgie” and “Peachie.”

From 1943 to 1946, Horgie served overseas with the 48th Highlanders of Canada while his young wife Peachie waited for him at home in Parkdale.

Through the UK, Italy, Belgium, Holland and Germany, he kept writing. 48highlanders 

More than 300 letters crossed the Atlantic — carrying the love, humour, fear and hope of a Toronto couple separated by war. 

Decades later, their grandson Rob Horgan transformed those letters into The November Project.

On Wednesday, October 7, Rob brings their story back to the Rivoli stage through readings from the original correspondence, accompanied by Eve Goldberg and a ukulele ensemble performing songs from the era. egoldberg

🎵📽️Be the first to view Wavelength: 25 Years of Music & Community, a short documentary telling the story of Toronto’s unique artist-run concert series and non-profit organization. Founded in 2000, Wavelength has grown from its roots as a weekly Sunday night club-show series and monthly photocopied zine, to a multi-format platform including outdoor festival experiences, thought-provoking conversations, and diversely curated concert presentations — while never wavering from its original vision of building more excitement for the grassroots Toronto music scene.

Written and directed by Ian Daffern Idfactoryfilms 
Director of Photography by Sheldon Norton sen69

Truly a community effort, this project features interviews with industry icons such as xmadmx + charlesspearin + itsmepagliacci + emilie.theaux , and music by moonbean_music richaucoin huge_luge sookyinleee

Scored and mixed by Justin Small justin_g_small ( DoMakeSayThink , BODY///GRAVE) and music supervised by Babs V. Westerholm ( CueQueensMusic )

⭐️In anticipation of Ace of Wands’ return to Wavelength, lead vocalist Lee Rose has put together an exclusive playlist for Wavelength! Here’s what she had to say about the song selection:

In making this playlist, I was thinking about how musical influence is rooted first in your direct community. There’s something interesting to me about how we absorb art made by others -  the way it trickles down into our own creative process, like a filter or a lense colouring how we see things. There’s a sympathetic relationship to how your friends and community members relate to your art, and how you relate to theirs. I feel like it can’t help colouring the sounds I write. I love thinking about how the process of new musical ideas is a cumulation of experience, directly impacted by the presence of others. No art is made in a vacuum. 

A lot of the songs on this list are made by artists we love, and are an extension of the Ace of Wands universe:

Jody now plays drums in the band Tumble, and while he isn’t playing on this recording, I can still hear him in there. TOVI is the project of one of my dearest friends Rebecca Emms, and she and I talk endlessly about how we create art and make this insane industry work. The Cross Sea is Anna’s solo music project, the epic fuzz tones on “Alien” feel like an extension of her guitar work in Ace of Wands. And Ian Blurton’s new music with Future Now reflects back to me some of the production we dove into with him on our album “Future Wave”. 

I hope we can continue to make art this way, leaning into the community spaces that make it all so interesting to begin with.

Their five-song debut EP, Greatest Hits, was recorded with producer Adam Tune and released on vinyl in May 2026, a fitting format for two kids raised on records and loud guitars. A who’s who of Canadian music, this project was scored and mixed by Justin Small justin_g_small ( DoMakeSayThink , BODY///GRAVE) and music supervised by Babs V. Westerholm ( CueQueensMusic ) and features interviews with Melissa Auf der Maur xmadmx (Hole, SmashingPumpkins ), Emilie Hanskamp emilie.theaux , pHoenix Pagliacci itsmepagliacci , Charles Spearin charlesspearin ( BrokenSocialScene , Do Make Say Think), and Wavelength’s Jonathan Bunce jdovercourt (AKA Jonny Dovercourt). Additional music by Bursmusic , huge_Luge, MOONBEAN_music , Orbital_Ensemble, OhyeahPaulChin, Pony Da Look, RichAucoin, SookYinLeee and more. 

A follow up to 2023’s acclaimed Reimagining Music Venues Study, the launch of the “New Sounds, New Space” report explores different pathways for establishing community hubs for Toronto’s grassroots music community. With positive case studies on Hugh’s Room Live, It’s Ok* Studios, Small World Music and Primal Note Studios, the report shines light on Toronto’s post-COVID music venue landscape while pointing the way forward for imaginative new spaces. Funded by Canada.Council for the Arts “Seed” grant!

Join in on the conversation that shapes Toronto’s music culture from the ground up.

A Horse Named Friday is a chamber folk ensemble from Kitchener-Waterloo, Ontario. Propelled into motion by singer-songwriter Jo El-Deek, and influenced by genres such as alt country, folk rock, chamber, and art pop, their sound has expanded into a full-band dynamic chorus of catharsis that invites listeners to find a home within emotional turbulence.

Their debut album “The Marriage of Loneliness and continental Bliss”, released on April 14th 2026, is comprised of hearty instrumentation featuring intricate strings arrangements, steady melodic guitars, and flourishes of piano, banjo and synth, giving listeners the opportunity to reflect and transform along with the shifting arrangements and soundscapes.

🎤✨Coming to Wavelength on August 27: charlesspearin & the Local Singers with Fleshtone Aura

Charles Spearin is a genre-defying Canadian musician and sonic explorer, best known as a founding member of the influential bands Broken Social Scene and Do Make Say Think. Over the past two decades, he has helped shape the sound of post-rock and indie music through a blend of heartfelt experimentation and collaborative alchemy.

Spearin’s solo work continues pushes the boundaries of what music can be. His critically acclaimed project The Happiness Project blurred the line between speech and melody, transforming lighthearted interviews with neighbours into rich musical compositions. More recently, he has created large-scale works such as Music for 32 Phones Played Simultaneously, a participatory symphony in which the audience’s phones became instruments in a shared auditory experience.

Whether through intricate arrangements or ephemeral sound experiments, Spearin’s work invites listeners to hear the world differently—to find music in the everyday and the extraordinary alike.

A heartfelt congratulations as well to Alex Cuba on his historic 2026 JUNO win for Latin Music Recording of the Year — the very first time this category has been awarded. Over the years, Alex has helped pave the way for so many artists across the country, opening doors and building space for Latin music in Canada to truly thrive. A truly unique and authentic voice, his work has expanded how Canadian audiences understand Cuban music in all its richness, and continues to inspire artists across generations and genres.

media.caption:
Always a pleasure having local artist Tom Davey in the studio.  tomdaveyart.

We’ve been working with Tom for nearly eight years, helping reproduce his original artwork and produce high-quality Giclée prints that stay true to the colours and character of his paintings.

It’s great to see a long-standing working relationship continue, and to play a small part in bringing his work to a wider audience.

#TomDavey #TomDaveyArt #BathArtist #ArtReproduction #GicleePrinting

Over 10 years of working together.

It’s always a pleasure having hopeblamireartist in the studio.

We’ve been working with Hope for more than a decade, photographing and reproducing her artwork to create high-quality Giclée files and prints - including this 150x75cm canvas from a recent reproduction.

Hope uses her artwork across a whole range of products, from limited-edition Giclée prints to some pretty amazing pieces for her growing collection. Check out her work - www.hopeblamire.com

And there’s something particularly satisfying about seeing the process come full circle - from photographing the original artwork, to producing the reproduction to Hope signing the finished edition.

Here’s to another 10 years! 🙌

What looks like a simple photograph can be surprisingly difficult to reproduce accurately.

This 1890s photograph from a private collection needed careful lighting to capture the original print without reflections, while preserving the subtle tones and detail needed for a precise colour-matched digital file.

Quick BTS showing our elinchrom_ltd lighting and cambo.photographic studio stand set up. #gicleereproduction #artscanning #photorestoration

A closer look at some large wood engravings for hilarypaynterartist .
A recent studio session with the brilliant Hilary Paynter, photographing a selection of her large-scale wood engravings for a new book she’s currently working on.
The size and detail of these pieces made this a particularly interesting reproduction job - capturing them accurately so all that intricate engraving detail can translate beautifully into print.
Always a pleasure working with artists who are so passionate about their craft. #HilaryPaynter #WoodEngraving #Printmaking #FineArtPrinting #ArtReproduction

The detail in this artwork is incredible. 👌

A few shots from a recent print run for Bath artist falzoniart Michael Falzoni whose work is inspired by the intricate tradition of Indian miniature art.

There’s so much detail in Michael’s originals, and a huge amount of time goes into creating them. So when we photograph and reproduce his work, we take our time to make sure those fine details and subtle variations come through in the final Giclée print. 

Prints on Hahnemuhle Ultra Smooth hahnemuehle_uk 

Always a pleasure working on something this intricate.

#BathArtist #ArtReproduction #GicleePrinting #FineArtPrinting #ImageCentre

The biggest reproduction job we’ve ever undertaken.

110 pages. 16 metres. Over 100 years of history.

We’ve carefully digitised, restored and reproduced this incredible Great Western Railway map as a bound book for the Sandford Station Railway Heritage Centre - giving a remarkable piece of railway history a new life.

All printed on beautiful hahnemuehle_uk PhotoRag 188gsm.

#GicleePrinting #ArtReproduction #MapRestoration #GreatWesternRailway #GWR

Starting with an original acrylic painting, we created a colour-matched digital reproduction before producing a large run of archival giclée prints.

Everything is produced in-house, from reproduction through to printing, quality remains consistent from the first print to the last print.

#ArtReproduction #GicleePrinting #FineArtPrinting #ColourManagement #ArchivalPrints

A short film with Sally Muir about her work, studio process, upcoming dog show, prints and the story behind how it all started.

Great art deserves faithful reproduction.
Giclée prints produced using archival pigment inks on Hahnemühle PhotoRag 308gsm, one of the world’s most respected fine art papers. The soft matte surface and subtle texture make it ideal for capturing the depth and character of original artwork.
Each piece is carefully colour matched to the original, ensuring the print reflects the true tones, contrast and detail of the painting.
The result is a museum-quality reproduction that preserves the integrity of the artwork.
If you’re an artist looking to reproduce your work as high-quality prints, get in touch.

Not every restoration we do hangs on a wall.

This hand-painted Ludo board belonged to our client’s grandfather. Years of moisture and foxing had left it fragile - too delicate to keep using, too important to lose.
We photographed the original, carefully restored the artwork digitally, and produced an archival giclée print on heavyweight hahnemuehle_uk UltraSmooth PhotoRag, finished with a protective matte giclee varnish.
Now it can be enjoyed again, without risking the original.
Unusual family pieces are often the most meaningful. If you’re unsure whether something can be restored, just ask.

HQ: @evergreen_brick_works

media.caption:
Do you wish you could meander through more parks and green spaces in your neighbourhood? 

Evergreen spoke with Farida Zaman (fzamanart), Toronto-based author–illustrator, who shares that having great public spaces is essential to her creative process in observing nature and her surroundings—the language of colour in all seasons and the play of light at different times of the day. 

According to Farida, being in nature can also help with slowing down and taking up art as a mindfulness practice. When we allow ourselves to not rush the process, we are less judgmental and kinder to ourselves, which is an important mindset to hold as an artist so it’s important to have places in the city where we can go, relax and enjoy nature at all times. 

Read more about how Farida's lived experiences around the world have shaped her art and illustration style. Link in bio.

We had a blast at #AdaptationCanada2026, where our Senior Designer Heidi Campbell co-led a tour of three transformed torontodsb schoolyards—showcasing how Evergreen’s Climate Ready Schools framework can turn schoolgrounds into greener, more resilient and joyful places for people and nature.
 
Using the framework, each schoolground demonstrates how thoughtful design can:
 
🦋 Enhance biodiversity and climate resilience
🌱 Support children’s development and outdoor learning
💚 Create spaces for connection and community
 
Thank you to iclei_canada for creating space to share Evergreen’s work—and to everyone who joined us on the tour!

🔗 Read the full press release at link in bio.

The extreme weather event that swept through the GTA on September 2 brought almost a month’s worth of rain (100mm) in a single day. The storm marks the second so-called “100-year” flood to affect Toronto in just two years, underscoring the need to rethink how cities define and prepare for extreme weather risk. 

Like many places in Toronto, Evergreen Brick Works flooded. But here, the site is designed with flooding in mind, and the aftermath of the storm is proving more manageable than it might have otherwise been. It holds important lessons for public infrastructure across the country.

Back-to-school season is here! For students at a school in East Gwillimbury, Ontario, there’s something new waiting for them.🌿

In partnership with yorkregiongovt and yorkcatholic_dsb, Evergreen is helping bring a new outdoor classroom to life.

The school ground at Our Lady of Good Counsel Catholic Elementary School was typical of many school grounds: a large open area with little shade, few trees or places for outdoor learning. The new outdoor classroom will create a shaded, natural setting where students can read, write, make art, study science, observe nature or simply spend time outdoors.

“The goal is to create a space that becomes part of everyday school life,” says Michael Ormston-Holloway, Evergreen’s design consultant on the project. “It will also become a community asset, especially because school grounds are often used outside school hours.”

This project builds on the approach behind Evergreen’s Climate Ready Schools program, using nature-based solutions to bring shade, biodiversity, outdoor learning and climate resilience to another school ground.

Do you instinctively head outside for a walk when you’re feeling stressed? There’s science behind that.

Long before co-founding Canada’s national nature prescription program, drmelissalem experienced those health benefits herself through time spent in the mountains, by the ocean and even at Evergreen Brick Works.

Wanting to get the story out, evergreencanada was the very first organization she worked with to turn that knowledge into action.

Fast forward to today, and through healthybynature.ca, an initiative of bcparksfdn, more than 20,000 regulated health professionals across Canada are prescribing time in nature, with more than two million nature prescriptions issued to date.

Read more about how a personal connection with nature turned into a national nature prescription program. 🔗 link in bio

Across Canada, a growing number of educators, outdoor leaders and health professionals are advocating for risky play: outdoor activities like climbing and jumping, using tools like knives for whittling or even learning to light fires.

In our latest video, we explore what risky play looks like at Evergreen Brick Works and how it helps kids build confidence, resilience and real-world decision-making skills. 

Watch the video on YouTube (link in bio) and subscribe to our channel to see upcoming risky play video guides.

What do we mean when we say Placekeeping?

As a national non-profit transforming public spaces across Canada, it’s critical that our work starts by understanding places. That means working with communities to honour the histories, ecologies and knowledge already rooted there.

Award-winning Métis landscape architect Terence Radford, Principal at trophicdesign and long time Evergreen Design Consultant, puts it this way:

“We’re allowing the land to lead and we’re honouring that place. We’re doing Placekeeping by working with a site rather than trying to fight it.”

Terence and his team often begin by looking back at a place’s history and ecology—including pre-colonial conditions—to understand what existed there long before current development. That research helps reveal how a site has changed over time before imagining its future.
 
We’re reflecting on how public spaces can be shaped through respect, reciprocity and care.

For this month’s #StaffSpotlight, meet Alison Scheuermann, Lead Event Manager at Evergreen! Alison ensures the seamless planning and execution of private event bookings at Evergreen Brick Works, ranging from weddings to family celebrations and corporate conferences. Let’s get to know more about her!

🐢 Share 3 fun facts about yourself! 

1. In May 2025, I adopted a dog from Korea who has completely stolen my heart. Gordita keeps me busy with daily walks and outdoor adventures, rain, or shine. 

2. I love being in nature—hiking, paddleboarding, and canoeing. This fall will be my 12th annual backcountry canoe trip with a close friend, a tradition we’ve kept since university. 

3. I’ve been lucky to travel extensively, including a nine-month backpacking trip through Central and South America, with more adventures still ahead. 

🐢 How do you make sure events at Evergreen Brick Works are sustainable? 

We embed sustainability into every event through clear standards. High-impact items like balloons, diesel generators, and single-use plastics are not permitted to reduce waste and emissions. We prioritize vendors with strong sustainability practices, including ethical sourcing and low-impact operations. We are currently working on a more effective recycling and composting program as well. 

🐢 What is your favorite thing about working at Evergreen Brick Works? 

There are a few things that stand out. First and foremost, the people. I truly value my team and the broader Evergreen community—I’ve always felt genuinely supported by those around me. The organization attracts thoughtful people, which really resonates with me. 

I also appreciate that, unlike much of the hospitality industry, the events we host directly support meaningful community programs and impact-driven work. 

And of course, the setting itself is a constant highlight. Being surrounded by nature, whether it’s greenery outside the office window or spotting turtles on a quick walk, adds something special to every day.

media.caption: In honour of Remembrance Day and National Indigenous Veterans Day, join Natalie Ortiz (natymocs) for a meaningful afternoon of beading, reflection, and remembrance on Saturday, November 7. In this hands-on workshop, participants will create a beautiful beaded poppy while learning about the significance of poppies as symbols of remembrance and the important contributions and sacrifices of Indigenous veterans. Register now on our website 🎟️

Join us for an evening of sketching the incredible footwear and fashion on display throughout the museum this Friday, October 9 from 5:00 - 9:00 pm. Whether you’re an experienced artist or just looking to try something new, this relaxed drop-in program offers a perfect blend of art, atmosphere, and imagination.

Did you know? Every second Friday of the month until the end of 2026, we will remain open until 9 pm for all to enjoy, with special free programming new each week plus access to all current exhibitions.

Celebrate the opening of our fall exhibition, Brilliant: The Art of Beaded Footwear around the World — an exhibition spanning 400 years of history and five corners of the globe, from Indigenous North America and West Africa to South and Southeast Asia, Europe, and Western fashion. Opens on Thursday, October 22 ✨

Join us on Sunday, October 25 for a full afternoon of family-friendly fun, with guided tours through over 85 extraordinary objects, hands-on beading crafts for all ages, and conversations with artists who have dedicated their practice to this meticulous, centuries-old art form.

Pictured: A Flower in a Desert, Manolo Blahnik x Mimi Plange Studio collaboration. Collection of mimiplange, New York.

Unboxing: Beaded Men’s Loafers ✨

Today we’re unboxing a pair of men’s loafers designed by Donald Pliner that will be featured in our upcoming exhibition Brilliant: The Art of Beaded Footwear Around the World. On view starting October 22, this exhibition traces the global history of beadwork through exceptional examples of beaded footwear from Africa, Europe, South Asia, Turtle Island (North America), and Western Asia.

The Bata Shoe Museum is pleased to present the annual Founder’s Lecture on Tuesday, November 10, featuring special guest Charles Miers, Publisher and Editorial Director of rizzolibooks imprints, in conversation with BSM Director and Senior Curator, elizabethsemmelhack, as they explore the intricate art of visual storytelling and the editorial vision behind some of the most celebrated fashion, design, and cultural books produced today. Purchase your tickets on our website today 🎟️

Learn more about this Roman footwear style that was popular for use in bathhouses. This example was embellished with lines marking where the toes sat and the leather strap was decorated with a serrated edge and an incised geometric pattern.

Collection of Vindolanda Trust, ca. 140-180 CE. Currently on view in our Unearthing Vindolanda exhibition, in partnership with officialvindolandatrust

SOLE STORIES with texas_traditions_boots

✨ NEW EXHIBITION ✨ 
Brilliant: The Art of Beaded Footwear Around the World opens on Thursday, October 22, 2026.

Beads are a popular form of ornamentation found on footwear around the world. Spanning 400 years of history, this exhibition brings together more than 85 meticulously crafted objects to illuminate both the delicate nature of beadwork and the exceptional effort, care, and skill it demands. Across diverse traditions, beads have been used in both decorative and symbolic ways, expressing status, identity, and spirituality. Brilliant traces the global history of beadwork through exceptional examples of beaded footwear from Africa, Europe, South Asia, Turtle Island (North America), and Western Asia.

Curated by elizabethsemmelhack, Director and Senior Curator, Bata Shoe Museum; nishib21, Curator and Manager of Exhibitions, Bata Shoe Museum; and Justine Woods, Assistant Professor, Parsons School of Design, The New School

Puma was founded by Rudolf Dassler in 1948. Puma’s first football boot, the 1950s ATOM, was very successful, but it was the launch of the SUPER ATOM in 1952 that changed the game. In collaboration with West Germany’s national soccer coach, Sepp Herberger, Puma developed the world’s first soccer boot with screw-in studs.

As part of our Soccer Spotlight, we have a pair of the 1952 Puma Super Atom (replicas from 1996), on loan from the Puma Archives on view until July 19 ⚽👟

Barry Ace’s sculptural assemblage, Gwiiwzens Dreamed of Spirit Horses, featuring his signature electronic component and glass bead medicine flower motifs, draws parallels to the colonial histories of Canada through material and metaphor. The Ojibwe Spirit Horse, also known as the Lac La Croix Pony, was driven to the point of extinction. In 1977 the four remaining mares were bred with Spanish Mustang stallions to preserve this critically endangered breed. The work consists of a pair of gifted children’s cowboy boots that rest on top of two vintage stylized galloping silver horse cobbler shoe rests. Wire trail dusters extend out from the back of the boots referencing the erasure of the Ojibwe Spirit Horse and fostering public awareness of the brutal colonial history that attempted to eradicate them. The title of the work implies an element of optimism for the future, as Gwiiwzens (the young boy) dreamed of the return of these Spirit Horses. Barry Ace is a multidisciplinary Odawa artist currently living in Ottawa. He is a member of M’Chigeeng (pronounced: She-ging) First Nation from Manitoulin Island in Ontario, Canada. 

On view in our Rough & Ready: A History of the Cowboy Boot exhibition.

As Perugia's reputation grew, he began to design footwear for some of the most famous singers, actors, and performers of the 1920s. He dressed Josephine Baker, Mistinguette, and Andrée Spinelli both on and off the stage. In one article from 1926, Mistinguette is proudly pictured with her collection of over 90 pair of Perugia shoes. This pair of vibrant and form-fitting turquoise boots were custom made for the famous actress Spinelli.

Collection of the Bata Shoe Museum. On view in our exhibition André Perugia: A Design Legend Unveiled.

🚨New Cocktail Class🚨

These are the “Oddballs.” The nerds. The “indoor” kids. The ones that you knew were awkward af but were gonna grow up to have their highschool bully as their gardener….maybe we're projecting. 

The point is: these cocktails have all struggled to find their footing in the stratosphere that is modern cocktail culture. 

The Rise N’ Shine, which is our very delicious take on an Espresso Martini, has had a hard time growing up - it doesn’t have a coffee liqueur in it. Or a father to look up to. And everyone and their mother thinks they're a connoisseur of Espresso Martinis. 

The Negroni is already an acquired taste - knows everything about everything but won’t shut up. When Ni9 said we made our own Ni9 Negroni… people were skeptical and curious… but skeptical to say the least. 

And finally, Whisky Business, our Whisky Sour using a very peculiar mystery cordial….has also walked uphill when it comes to cocktail menus - people are very fussy about their Whisky Sours and guess what….so are bartenders.

So, we invite you to put our “Oddballs” in the spotlight and let them know how appreciative we are for their continued efforts. Just don’t drink them “performatively” like that Bay Street bro you know that won’t shut up about how he now suddenly loves Negronis.

✨ THREE EXPERIENCES • ONE ROOF ✨
Meet your new go-to spot in the Junction:

🍻 Samara Brewing Co. - Our craft brewery and newest addition, where every brew and every sip tells a story connecting happy community to happy taste buds. From rich red ales to juicy New England IPAs, there’s a beer for every palate. With the coolest titles like Dispersion, Spinning Jenny, Acer, and Wind Driven - we've got beer names that’ll make you downright "hoppy"!

🍸 Nickel 9 Distillery – Toronto’s distillery with love. All spirits are crafted in-house by our master distiller, Greg. From vodka to oak-aged spirits to liqueurs- we make ’em all, we’ve got ’em all, and we craft the most stunning cocktails with them. Did we mention that we make all our cocktail syrups and bitters in-house, too? We'd list them here, but frankly, there are just too many - it would be easier if you stopped by and checked them out yourself 😏.

🍽️ Stav’s Corner – Dine-in magic and event catering straight from the brilliant mind of Chef Stav. Serving up a variety of foods with vegan and plant-based options that’ll blow your mind- the vegan gravy is phenomenal, the fries are crispy, crunchy, oh-so-good, the hummus and pitas are fresh, and the butternut squash ravioli? More like ravi-holy! Every bite is fan-pasta-c!

From casual nights out to milestone moments, we’re your all-in-one destination for unforgettable food, drinks, and celebrations. ❤️

Think we’ve got limits? Challenge us.

media.caption:
MESKEL BAYRAMI 🇪🇹

Meskel, Etiyopya’nın yüzyıllardır yaşattığı en önemli dini ve kültürel geleneklerden biridir. Etiyopya Ortodoks inancına göre bayram, İmparatoriçe Helena’nın Hz. İsa’nın çarmıhının bulunduğu yeri keşfetmesinin hatırasını yaşatır.

Meskel’in en etkileyici geleneği Demera adı verilen büyük ateşin yakılmasıdır. İnsanlar ateşin çevresinde bir araya gelir; dualar, ilahiler ve kutlamalarla bu kadim geleneği nesilden nesile taşır.

መልካም የመስቀል በዓል!
ለኢትዮጵያ ሕዝብ ሁሉ ሰላም፣ ፍቅርና ደስታ ይሁን። 🇪🇹
Etiyopya dan Mutlu pazarlar sevgili Türk halkı 🇹🇷🫶🏼🇪🇹
Bir kere alıştın mı bırakamazsın. Yemeyen bilmez; injera bağımlılık yapar. 🇪🇹❤️🇹🇷

Etiyopya’da ritmi sadece müzikte duymazsın, görürsün de. 🇪🇹💃🏾😄
Geleneksel dansların en güzel tarafı: bazen bütün hikâyeyi omuzlar ve baş anlatır.

In Ethiopia, you don’t just hear the rhythm — you see it. 🇪🇹💃🏾😄
Sometimes the shoulders and the head tell the whole story.

🇹🇷🫶🇪🇹

🐾 INTERNATIONAL DOG DAY — AUGUST 26

Come hold a puppy. Leave with something a little bigger. 💛

Recent stories of animals being harmed — including cases involving children and teenagers — have stayed with us and made us ask:

How can we nurture empathy and respect for animals from a young age?

We can't solve animal cruelty with one puppy event. But we can use International Dog Day to do something positive in our own community.

This August 26, we're welcoming a group of Corgi puppies to Yoga Kawa for an afternoon of Puppy Yoga, our Kids Puppy Cuddle & Care Club, and a relaxing Puppy Cuddle Sound Bath.

🐶 During our Kids Puppy Cuddle & Care Club, children will learn how to gently interact with puppies, understand their body language and boundaries, care for dogs, and help protect animals in their community — with puppy trivia, face painting and plenty of cuddles along the way.

And throughout the day, our puppies will have dedicated rest, nap, water and potty breaks because their wellbeing always comes first. 💤🐾

💛 $5 from each main experience ticket will be donated to the Justice for Animals Foundation in support of animal protection.

If even a few children leave thinking a little more about what an animal needs, rather than only what we want from an animal, that's worthwhile.

Raise empathy early.
Raise a kinder generation. 🐾💛

📅 Tuesday, August 26
📍 Yoga Kawa | 539A Mt Pleasant Rd, Toronto

this Nuit Blanche (nuitblancheto), we’re opening the door to the world of Toronto artist Lynn Donoghue (lynndonoghueestate) 🎨⁠
⁠
on oct 3, our Modern Wing Lobby becomes a window into Donoghue’s world, with her studio brought back to life as it was left in 2003. a selection of works, unseen for more than two decades, is coming out of storage and into view once again.⁠
⁠
Donoghue spent years painting the artists, creatives and characters around Roncesvalles and Dundas, capturing a community that was often overlooked and bringing their stories into focus through colour, scale and an unflinching gaze. works like Alex and the Perfect Blue Sky offer a glimpse into the world Donoghue was capturing nearly 50 years ago.⁠
⁠
come step inside her studio in the Modern Wing Lobby for Nuit Blanche, and see more of Donoghue’s work at Art Toronto this fall.⁠

December 2nd!

 Forget the Nutcracker. For a real taste of seasonal cheer, nothing says joy to the world like Bill Kirchen singing Daddy's Drinkin' Up Our Christmas.  Featured is a sleigh-full of rarely heard holiday numbers from the blues, rock 'n' roll and honky tonk bags: Silent Surfin' Night, Truckin' Trees for Christmas, Santa Looked A Lot Like Daddy and many more. But be ye not afraid, there'll be so much more than holiday songs of questionable taste; you can count on a truckload of dieselbilly classics to take the edge off the holiday fuss. Bill will be touring with his all-star Texas band The Silent Knights (Jack Saunders on bass and Rick Richards on drums).

🎃 2000s HALLOWEEN PARTY 👻

Get ready to throw it back to the era of flip phones, MySpace, low-rise jeans, burned CDs, and the absolute best party anthems of the 2000s, with a Halloween twist.
On October 30, Lee’s Palace transforms into a spooky throwback party packed with the biggest hits, guilty pleasures, and dance-floor classics from the 2000s.
👻COME IN COSTUME
Go all out. Your favourite 2000s icon, horror movie villain, pop star, emo legend, celebrity, or whatever weird creation you can dream up.
🏆 BEST DRESSED PRIZES
Think your costume has what it takes? We’ll be handing out prizes throughout the night for the best-dressed partygoers.
🪩 2000s MUSIC ALL NIGHT
From pop and hip-hop to emo, pop-punk, R&B and everything in between. Expect the songs you grew up with and the ones you forgot you knew every word to.
🎃 SPOOKY VIBES
Halloween decorations, creepy surprises, throwback visuals and a full night of nostalgic party energy.

Grab your friends, dig through that closet, and get ready for the ultimate 2000s Halloween throwback.

media.caption: Друзья! Мы заканчиваем масштабный косметический ремонт, установили новый звук от L-Acoustics, оборудовали сцену огромным экраном 6*3,5м и концертным светом. А теперь самое главное — MOD меняет своё название на Рассвет. Мы работаем над сменой айдентики и уже запустили новый сайт rassvet.place, где постепенно будет появляться всё больше анонсов. Следите за обновлениями и оставайтесь с нами. Встретим рассвет вместе ❤️

Друзья! Мы приближаемся к Новому году и хотим поздравить вас с наступающими праздниками. В 2025 году нас ждут большие изменения: в MOD пришла новая и сильная команда. Мы уже начали делать ремонт, поменяли свет и звук. В общем, доводим пространство до ума, чтобы каждый концерт был комфортным и запоминающимся не только за счёт любимых артистов, но и благодаря самой площадке. Также в будущем нас ждёт смена названия и концепции, которые обретут новый яркий смысл. Постепенно мы будем рассказывать о всех изменениях и развиваться в лучшую сторону. Надеемся на вашу поддержку: ведь какой же театр без зрителя! 
 
В то же время желаем вам не бояться и не сдаваться, крепкого здоровья, вселенской любви! Найдите свою цель и не забывайте о мечтах. Оставайтесь такими, какие вы есть – ведь каждый из вас уникален! С Новым 2025 годом!

🥐 Breakfast is served. We'll take one order of this buttery brioche painted by Manet, s'il vous plaît, merci! 🥐
Also on the menu all the other delightful works on view in The Impressionist Revolution: Monet to Matisse from the Dallas Museum of Art.
Interestingly, despite the close relationships Manet had with many of the Impressionist members, he declined to exhibit with them and continued submitting his work to the state-run Salon instead. Nevertheless, he remained open to their artistic innovations and adopted their bright, pastel palette and interest in rendering light effects, as seen in this airy still life. 
Come see it soon - the last day to see the exhibition is October 18!

It's the last weekend to see Painted Presence: Rembrandt and his Peers,a remarkable selection of seventeenth century Dutch paintings. Shown in dialogue with paintings from the AGO’s European Collection of Art, at the centre of this focused installation are seven artworks attributed to Rembrandt van Rijn (1606-1669), shown together for the first time. Featuring intensely observed still life paintings, detailed interiors and mesmerizing portraits, these striking artworks offer a rare glimpse of Dutch artistry at work.
This exhibition is co-organized by the Art Gallery of Ontario and the Agnes Etherington Art Centre, Queen's University.
The last day to see the show is Sunday, October 4.

In The Impressionist Revolution: Monet to Matisse from the Dallas Museum of Art you'll see not just some favourite Impressionist artworks, but also how the movement impacted two successive generations of avant-garde painters.
For example, Edvard Munch initially experimented with Impressionism, but he felt its emphasis on naturalism did not allow the emotional expression he sought. Munch developed his unique Expressionist style through his use of sinuous line and exaggerated colour. Here, he depicts a recently deforested area in the Thuringian Forest in Germany. With boldly contrasting complementary colours—red and green—he portrays the undulating landscape as bleeding and raw to convey feelings of anguish and despair.
Come see this, and all the others on view now. Start your weekend here - we're open until 9 pm on Fridays!

The AGO mourns the passing of Yayoi Kusama (March 22, 1929 – August 14, 2026). For more than 70 years, Kusama has invited people to participate in her groundbreaking visions of infinity. This prolific experimental artist was an internationally acclaimed art world icon, with her work being shown across the globe. 
You came in droves – and even lined up around the block – to see Yayoi Kusama: Infinity Mirrors in 2018, making it one of the AGO’s most popular exhibitions. Following the show, thanks to the generosity of over 4,700 #InfinityAGO donors who participated in our crowdfunding campaign and the David Yuile & Mary Elizabeth Hodgson Fund, the AGO became the permanent home of INFINITY MIRRORED ROOM - LET’S SURVIVE FOREVER. Every day we hear moments of pure delight and excitement from the work as visitors experience the magic of an Infinity Mirrored Room for the first (or 100th) time. 
Kusama added whimsy, and a lot of awe into the world with her art. If you’ve experienced one of her works, you’re likely to remember it forever. We’re infinitely grateful for the legacy she leaves and the way her art has moved visitors here in Toronto, and across the globe.

Mulock House was built in 1871 and is located within Mulock Park, a 16-acre green space in Newmarket, just north of the GTA.  Designated under the Ontario Heritage Act, the Town of Newmarket has preserved, updated, and reimagined the home and its park, transforming it into a community hub with a café, restored lounge in Sir William Mulock’s library, gathering spaces, and a 2,000-sq.-foot art gallery.

Beverly Glenn-Copeland’s “Light of the Heavens” is now on at MOCA as part of our South Stairwell Sound Series.

Resonating throughout the stairwell, the recently recovered song from his archives was created during the same era as his landmark album “Keyboard Fantasies,” which celebrates its 40th anniversary this fall.

Untethered to any album, the song embodies the contemplative spirit and sonic language that has drawn generations of listeners, including more recent admirers and collaborators Sam Smith, Bon Iver, Romy, and Wu Tsang, among others.

A mysterious blend of synthesizers supports Glenn-Copeland’s tender, measured voice, evoking both the immeasurable expanse of the universe and the reassuring sense of our belonging within it.

Described by him as “a gift from my past,” the song sheds new light on Glenn-Copeland’s enduring practice while offering a meditation on the ties between humanity and the unknowable.

Bharti Kher’s exhibition "Bones" is now on view at MOCA. 

"Bones" brings together new and earlier sculpture from the past 15 years in a dynamic dialogue with the Auto BLDG. The works move between the bodily, the architectural, and the cosmic, creating a shifting world of support and suspension, where surreal female goddesses intertwine with geometric and spiralling forms. Some of the figures are draped in Indian saris, while others float within the surrounding abstract elements.

Throughout her practice, Kher has explored how the body, shape, and sacred geometries interact and shift our understanding of the world around us. "Bones" balances control and instability in a constant tension, as her forms resist the need to settle and yet seem to find an equilibrium.

Kher's "Matter" paintings, also on view, present mirrored fields of bindis in formations evoking a celestial sky.

October 4, 2026–February 14, 2027

📷  Bharti Kher, "Bones," installation view, MOCA Toronto, 2026. Photo: LF Documentation.

Delcy Morelos’s newly commissioned, site-specific installation stretches and swells from the ceiling, illuminated by natural light. Among Morelos’s most ephemeral large-scale works to date, it follows the contours of a womb and is woven from long strands of sisal rope treated with soil and corn roots harvested in Toronto.

Embedded with mixtures of corn, tapioca, and tobacco, the earth recalls the medicinal and nourishing roles of these plants in the Americas. Through its physical presence, fragrance, and texture, "Ombligo" creates a space for reflection on sustenance, ritual, migration, extraction, and restoration.

October 4, 2026–February 14, 2027

It’s corn! 🌽

For Delcy Morelos’s upcoming exhibition “Ombligo,” we partnered with Crooked Farmz, a Toronto-based microfarm at Downsview Park, to grow more than 1,000 stalks of corn for her newly commissioned installation.

Led by Sean Smith, Crooked Farmz is rooted in a commitment to soil health, urban agriculture, and our connection to the land. Sean’s practice centres on composting, microbial life, and sustainable food systems. Together with Ratcliff Farms, he planted, nurtured, harvested, and dried the corn, whose roots are now part of Morelos’s monumental installation.

The local collaboration reflects Morelos’s ongoing exploration of our relationship with the earth.

MOCA's South Stairwell Sound Series returns with a new work by music legend Beverly Glenn-Copeland.

Titled "Light of the Heavens," the piece is a recently recovered song from Glenn-Copeland's archives, something he calls “a gift from my past.” Created in the mid eighties, the song echoes a quieter chapter of his life on the Canadian Shield. It's shimmering, weightless, and carried by his tender voice, as he sings “by the guiding stars, the cosmic veil, we are ever coming home to the light of the heavens.”

A visionary composer, trans elder, and classically trained musician, his five-decade career continually evolves, spanning folk, electronic, and spiritual music. This project comes just ahead of the reissue of his landmark 1986 album “Keyboard Fantasies,” which celebrates its 40th anniversary this fall.

Experience it October 4 in MOCA's South Stairwell.

This fall, MOCA is excited to present "Bones," a major solo presentation by acclaimed artist Bharti Kher. 

Kher is known for her approach to assemblage, where she builds her work by breaking apart and reconstituting found materials and castings, a process she describes as a way to "know them better."

"Bones" gathers Kher's surreal female figures, some draped in saris, others entwined with spiraling forms. She's described these beings as “mythical urban goddesses” who are, “part truth, and part fiction, part me, and part you.” Nearby, geometric works in wood, stone, and concrete stand alongside a new large-scale painting built from thousands of hand-applied bindis.

Born in London and based in New Delhi since 1993, Kher’s work arrives at MOCA following two milestone UK exhibitions: "Alchemies," a major solo show of sculpture staged across Yorkshire Sculpture Park, and a current display at the V&A in London, where her work stands in dialogue with the museum's collection of classical sculpture.

Opening October 4. Link in bio to learn more.

This fall, MOCA is thrilled to unveil Delcy Morelos's "Ombligo," a major site-specific commission woven from sisal rope treated with soil and corn roots harvested in Toronto. 

Suspended from the ceiling on Floor 2 and illuminated by natural light, the form follows the contours of a womb. Pulling inspiration from the ingenuity of the spider, delcymorelos spins and weaves a sensory web that binds, catches, shelters, and nurses. 

Rooted in her relationship to the land in her native Colombia, Morelos works earth and organic materials into installations that engage scent and touch. 

She carried that same practice through a remarkable summer, including "origo," a monumental 24-metre outdoor commission at London's Barbican, and "Madre," a fragrant, immersive installation staged in dialogue with Joseph Beuys at Berlin's Hamburger Bahnhof.

"Ombligo" opens at MOCA on October 4.

“In Korea, we have an expression, ‘to wrap a bottari,’ which means leaving home and family behind to begin one’s own life.” — Kimsooja

On Floor 1, found textiles hang from the ceiling, while bottari bundles made of household sheets and personal garments are planted firmly on the ground, quiet witnesses to the lives that have touched them. 

As you move through the space between them, you’re invited into Kimsooja’s enduring exploration of migration, movement, and what we carry forward as we leave one life behind.

🔎 Sara Cwynar transforms our outdoor Lightbox with "Encyclopedia Grid, Women Demonstrating Technology."

Drawing from illustrations accompanying the same encyclopedia entry across different editions and languages, Cwynar traces which images were repeated, changed, or replaced over time. Reconciliation is not a day on the calendar. It is an ongoing, living responsibility.
 
What does that responsibility look like for each of us?
 
For former Harbourfront Centre Artist-in-Residence Marissa Magneson, it starts with learning. With listening. With asking questions. And with finding meaningful ways to participate in reconciliation that makes sense in our own lives.
 
Her installation, Ribbons of (Re)conciliation, brings the Truth and Reconciliation Commission’s 94 Calls to Action into view, creating a living work that will continue to evolve as progress is made.
 
Earlier this year, we sat down with Marissa to learn more about her work and perspective. We gathered some of her words on why the Calls to Action matter, what September 30th represents, and how we can each begin to take part in reconciliation.
 
And this is just part of the conversation. Keep an eye out for our full interview with Marissa, coming soon in the weeks ahead.
 
Visit Ribbons of (Re)conciliation in our main lobby and return throughout the year to see how it changes. Because, hopefully, it won’t be the same work the next time you see it.

Harbourfront Centre’s main building at 235 Queens Quay West will be temporarily closed from October 5–18 while we complete a major phase of our energy retrofit project.
 
During this time, public access to the main building will be restricted, including the Ontario Science Centre at Harbourfront Centre and Boxcar Social. P2 parking will remain open, although occasional delays are possible.
 
The work is part of a larger project to replace aging infrastructure, improve building reliability and reduce our greenhouse gas emissions by approximately 50 per cent.

Sometimes we’re so used to moving through the city that we forget to really experience it.

But a city is more than its buildings, streets and busy schedules. It’s the people who fill it, and the moments that make us stop, get curious, slow down, have some fun, hear someone else’s story or see a familiar place a little differently.

Public art creates those moments, giving us something new to notice, question, enjoy or connect with, turning the places we pass through into places we participate in.

Here’s to the art that makes our campus a little more curious, playful and human 💙

Reconciliation isn’t a moment.

It isn’t just one day on the calendar.

It’s an ongoing responsibility — one that requires learning, listening, accountability and action.

Residential schools were part of a broader system of colonial policies intended to assimilate Indigenous Peoples.

In 2008, the Truth and Reconciliation Commission of Canada was established following the Indian Residential Schools Settlement Agreement. It heard testimony from Survivors and documented the history and ongoing impacts of the residential school system. 
In 2015, the TRC released its final report and 94 Calls to Action — a framework for addressing the legacy of residential schools and advancing reconciliation.

The Calls to Action are specific, but their message is clear. We’ve pulled out some of the recurring priorities across the Calls and we encourage you to read the Calls themselves, learn from Indigenous voices and consider what reconciliation asks of you.

For Harbourfront Centre, reconciliation means continuing to work with, present and promote Indigenous artists and their practices while continuing to learn and examine our own role as an arts and cultural institution.

🔗 Read the 94 Calls to Action in full through the link in our bio, and consider how you can continue learning, listening and taking action toward reconciliation.

🏡 Thank you to our generous supporters! We're steps closer to building a new home for Bad Dog!

For more than 40 years, Bad Dog has been a place where people found creativity, confidence, friendship, artistic opportunity, and community.

Now, we’re working toward something bigger: A permanent home for comedy and improvisation in Toronto.

It’s about building a home for:
❤️ comedy and creativity
❤️ late-night conversations
❤️ classes and rehearsals
❤️ artists finding their voice
❤️ audiences gathering together
❤️ the next generation of Toronto improv

If Bad Dog has ever made you laugh, introduced you to your people, helped you grow, or reminded you that you belong somewhere, we hope you’ll consider helping us build what comes next.

Build it with us Learn more at https://baddogtheatre.com/anewhome

PHYSICALITY FIRST

Chase Jeffels, Instructor
Sundays 3pm-5:30pm
November 8 - December 6 (5 Weeks)

Description: In this class by Chese Jeffels, students will explore the potential that opens up by leading with physicality. Students will learn techniques to expand their physical expression and use it to form characters, establish environments, and create the emotional framework on which they can build wonderful scenes.

Prerequisite: Improv Foundation 4 or equivalents.

About Chase: Chase Jeffels is an actor and comedian with a deep background in physical performance. His clown study brought him to France, where he trained with Ecole Jacques Lecoq, Laboratoire d'Étude du Mouvement, and Phillipe Gaulier. This training, combined with his training in traditional theatre and improv, has formed the basis of Chase's performance practice since - which includes extensive work in TV, film, and live comedy. Check out his work with acclaimed sketch collective $20 Sandwich.

SOLO CHARACTER CREATION FOR SKETCH & THEATRE

Curtis Campbell, Instructor
Sundays 3pm-5:30pm (2.5 Hours)
September 20 - October 25 (5 Weeks, No Class Oct 11)
CSI Spadina (192 Spadina Ave)

Description: On both the stage and social media, comedians are breaking through with solo character-based sketch comedy. It is an inexpensive way to use your performance skills in a way that expresses your point of view and reach a (potentially unlimited) audience. Learn why this format is so popular, and how to make it work for you.

Prerequisite: At least some performance and/or creative writing experience preferred.

Cost: $375+HST

Location: CSI Spadina (192 Spadina Ave)

About The Instructor: Curtis Campbell is an award-winning writer of novels, plays, and comedy. Their plays Gay For Pay and Blake & Clay's Gay Agenda received a Dora nomination for Best New Play, won the Second City Award for Outstanding Comedy, and have been published by Scirocco Drama. Their debut novel Dragging Mason County was selected for the White Raven List, was a finalist for the White Pine Award, and won a Publishing Triangle Award. Their new novel Lying, Stealing, And Other Ways To Save The Planet will be published in 2026 and is currently available for preorder. In addition to his writing practice, Curtis regularly teaches writing workshops for young adults.

Saturdays Noon-2:30pm (2.5 Hours)
November 7 - December 5 (5 Weeks)

Description: In this special offering from Becky Johnson, participants will learn how to use special techniques to help them unlock their creative potential. Through flash writing, the class will explore using impulse and their subconscious to expand their unique voice. Students will explore forms such as script writing (ie drama, sketch, etc.), poetry, and prose, as well as collaborative writing.

IMPROVISING FROM THE BODY: Building Scenes & Dynamic From Physical Impulse

Tuesdays 6pm-8:30pm (2.5 Hours)
November 10 - December 8 (5 Weeks)

Description: In this special offering from Becky Johnson, participants will learn to calm their thinking and use physical impulse to build improvised scenes and show structures. If you're an improvisor that sometimes finds yourself stuck during scenes, this class will help in developing new pathways that get you out of your head and into your body. This course will involve practicing both scenework and longer improv structures.

About Becky: Becky Johnson is an award-winning actor, writer, and a creator of all sorts of things for 20+ years. She is the recipient of multiple Canadian Screen Awards for her work on Baroness Von Sketch Show (CBC) and Space Riders (CTV). Her other work in television includes This Hour Has 22 Minutes (CBC) and The Amazing Gayl Pile (CBC Gem). In improv, she is best known as an alumna of The Second City Mainstage, as one half of two acclaimed duos - Iron Cobra (with Graham Wagner) and The Sufferettes (with Kayla Lorrette) - and as the long-time co-producer of Catch23. Her work in live comedy and theatre includes 3 Canadian Comedy Awards, 8 overall Canadian Comedy Award nominations, and a Dora Award nomination for the world premiere of Sheila Heti's All Your Happy Days Are Stupid.

DON'T THINK (IT'S SUPPOSED TO BE FUN)

Alex Cabrera-Aragon, Instructor
Sunday October 18 (3pm-5:30pm)
BAD DOG STUDIO (392 Spadina Ave)
$60+HST 

Description: If you're an improvisor that gets stuck in the moment, it's not because you can't think of anything - it's because you're thinking too much. In this workshop, students will learn techniques to help them stop overthinking and start feeling in the moment. Students will learn how to overcome their internal judgment, dive into the unknown, trust their scene partners, and feel the joy that comes from embracing true spontaneity. Whether you're in the process of learning improv for the first time or an experienced improvisor hoping to benefit from new techniques, this class is all about finding and enjoying the fun.

Prerequisite: Improv Foundation 1 or equivalents.

About The Instructor: Alex Cabrera-Aragon has been a writer and improvisor since 2014. As a member of Bad Dog's Feature Players Ensemble, she performed in the show People Of The City which debuted at Factory Theatre earlier this year and featured such special guests as Mayor Olivia Chow. Alex has also performed and toured with the troupes The Kids Table and Bruce. She studied screenwriting at TMU and under the mentorship of writer-producer Anthony Q. Ferrell (The Office, Run The Burbs).

Description: In this workshop, students will joyfully explore comedy in lyric form. Learn techniques to turn your point of view into songs or lyric poetry and discover how structure can influence your work.

Prerequisite: Improv Foundation 1 or equivalents. No prior musical or writing experience necessary.

About The Instructors: 

Maricris Rivera (she/her) is a Filipina-Canadian performer, producer, and creator. She is a member of the award-winning multidisciplinary ensemble, the Tita Collective. She is a composer for various children's music programs. You can find her at different open mics and jams across Toronto, and is currently working on her first album. 

Alia Rasul is an award-winning storyteller, writer / performer, and Bad Dog's Artistic Director. As a member of the all-Filipina group Tita Collective, Alia produces the Tawa Festival and has co-created several acclaimed stage revues. Besides her work with Tita Collective, Alia's live comedy works include collaborations with many of Canada's leading comedy artists as a producer, director, and dramaturge. Off-stage, she wrote and produced the documentary 15 Ways My Dad Almost Died (CBC Gem / Reel Asian Film Festival) and is the author of Super Important Filipina Thoughts (ANAK Publishing).

Thursdays 6pm-8:30pm (2.5 Hours)

Clownprov 1 blends elements found within clown work (physical comedy, le jeu, finding "the game", and joyful play) with improv. Participants will learn to maximize joy during performance; repeat and build off their successes, and access their "inner clown" within the context of improv scene work.

Goal: To blend the fundamental principles of clowning with scenic improvisation. This class includes an on-stage performance opportunity.

Prerequisite: Improv Foundation 3 or equivalent

Duration: 12 hours total - 6 weeks x 2 hours
Price: $375+HST
Class Size: 10 Maximum

Location: Bad Dog Studio (392 Spadina Ave)

About Your Instructor: Ken Hall is an award-winning actor, clown performer, comedian, and teacher - best known for his roles on Umbrella Academy (Netflix) and People Of Earth (TBS). When not acting in TV and film productions, Ken is active in Toronto’s performing arts communities. Ken is one half of the acclaimed duo 2-Man No-Show and has performed with such companies as Cirque Du Soleil, Young People’s Theatre, The Second City, Bad Dog Theatre Company, and CanStage. His accolades in theatre and comedy include Dora Award Nominations and Canadian Comedy Award wins.

Ken has taught improv, clown, and public speaking to students across the country. His teaching style draws from both his creative practice with comedy improvisation and clowning and his career background in social work and counselling. He remains one of the most popular instructors in the Bad Dog Community.

Holiday! An Improvised Musical takes its inspiration from Stephen Sondheim’s “Company” to bring you the only party you’ll need. Based on suggestions from the audience, the cast weaves together a series of improvised vignettes and songs exploring love, relationships, work and the true meaning of the season. Naomi Klein and Avi Lewis (Author, journalist, social activist, and filmmaker | Filmmaker, climate activist, educator)

Factory is so excited and proud to introduce two new faces to our team! Welcome to the building Sascha Cole, our new Artistic Producer, and Caroline John, our new Senior Manager of Philanthropy and Partnerships! Swipe to learn more about these lovely people ✨

ABOUT SASCHA 

Sascha Cole is a Dora-nominated actor and creative producer with 25 years of experience working across Canada’s arts and culture landscape. Her producing career has included international collaborations and presentations at large-scale festivals, alongside extensive work with independent artists. She brings a comprehensive perspective and deep love for the Toronto performing arts ecology, with a practice rooted in artistic development, collaboration, and creative risk. She is thrilled to join Factory in this moment of transformation.

“Sascha Cole is a producer and artist of the highest calibre, whose name and reputation in Toronto precedes her. I’m honoured that Sascha is offering her time and many talents to the Factory team.”

Kevin Matthew Wong, Artistic Director

Caroline John is a non-profit and fundraising professional with over 20 years of experience in the arts, culture, environment, public policy, and community service oriented organizations. She brings a breadth of knowledge and experience in driving success for the performing arts and the inter-related communities of artists, creatives, artsworkers, economies, and society.
