Kevin Matthew Wong, Artistic Director

Tickets are ON SALE NOW for “Provisions” and “What You Won’t Do For Love”, both part of Factory’s fall season. Get your tickets now at the link in our bio! ✨

What You Won’t Do For Love
October 21–22 2026
Starring David Suzuki and Tara Cullis
A Why Not Theatre production presented by Factory Theatre

“What’s love got to do with it?” A lot, according to David Suzuki.

After a lifetime devoted to climate activism, internationally-renowned environmentalists David Suzuki and Tara Cullis take to the stage in an intimate and inspiring theatre experience. A rare behind-the-scenes look at a life shaped by deep love, commitment, and the courage to act; they reflect on their extraordinary 50-year partnership in life and work.

Provisions
November 13–29 2026
A Lester Trips (Theatre) Production in Association with Factory Theatre
Created by Lauren Gillis & Alaine Hutton

Have you ever danced on the head of a pin? – the last text sent by the cast and crew of a failed reality tv show set on the moon before they stopped sending footage and went silent.

On earth, an ordinary broke person in the microgig economy accepts an odd job: accompany an agentic AI to the moon to retrieve the people and data from the failed lunar reality tv venture, and return them to earth before they suffocate. She soon discovers the inhabitants are not easily convinced to leave an erotic choose-your-own virtual reality simulation to board a space megabus back to burning earth. A secret VR love affair, a nun digging a gooneral, and all manner of bodily and metaphysical decomposition confirm suspicions that this gig extends far beyond occasionally assisting a bot with slippery door handles.

Did you hear the news? Kevin Matthew Wong is our new Artistic Director! 

Swipe through to learn more about Kevin and his vision for Factory as a world class home for creativity and presentation, and check out the link in our bio to support Factory Theatre and Kevin in this exciting new chapter.

Photo callmealbs

Introducing Factory Theatre’s new Artistic Director, Kevin Matthew Wong! We are thrilled to welcome Kevin, an internationally touring theatre creator, producer, and cultural leader, as he steps into this role leading Factory into a new chapter of rigorous, uplifting, and intimate performing arts at 125 Bathurst. 
 
Kevin’s appointment marks a new chapter for Factory Theatre that reimagines the institution as a world-class home for creativity while connecting Toronto with the world. Under Wong’s leadership, the company’s artistic vision will encompass theatre, dance, music, cabaret, film, Theatre for Young Audiences, devised performance and multidisciplinary creation. 

Kevin comes to Factory following seven years at Why Not Theatre, most recently as Executive Producer and Artistic Associate. There, he helped shape the company’s national and international work while leading a portfolio of large-scale and touring projects. Wong’s own creative work has been presented across Canada and internationally - his acclaimed Benevolence series explores Hakka identity, migration, guesthood and cultural inheritance across theatre, film and installation. 

Check out the link in our bio for the full announcement! 
 
Photo credit: callmealbs

There’s no better way to bring our fall 2026 programming to a raucous close than with the return of Bad Dog Theatre’s beloved Holiday! An Improvised Musical (December 10 – 19, 2026), in association with Factory Theatre.  
 
Holiday! takes its inspiration from Stephen Sondheim’s Company to bring you the only party you’ll need. Based on suggestions from the audience, the cast weaves together a series of improvised vignettes and songs exploring love, relationships, and the true meaning of the season. 
 
Factory season artwork by Mark Krzepis krzepism

In November, Factory will host the full world premiere of Provisions, a Lester Trips (Theatre) Production in association with Factory Theatre (November 13 – 29, 2026). Provisions will complete the award-winning, critically acclaimed body horror trilogy that began with the sold-out Honey I’m Home in 2024 and was followed by the Dora-winning Public Consumption in 2025! 

Crushed by the microgig economy, David accepts an odd job: accompany an agentic AI to an abandoned factory on the moon and retrieve the cast, crew, and data from a failed reality tv show before they all suffocate. (Meta)physical resistance gives way to ecstatic horror. Created by Lauren Gillis and Alaine Hutton. 
 
Factory season artwork by Mark Krzepis krzepism

In addition to our onstage offerings this fall, we’re so pleased to once again support Native Earth Performing Arts’ Weesageechak Begins to Dance 39 Workshop Stream, supporting projects in early stages of development for artists seeking to explore their project without the pressure of a public presentation.  
 
Weesageechak Begins to Dance is Native Earth Performing Arts’ annual performing arts festival showcasing new works and works-in-development by Indigenous artists across Turtle Island and beyond. Held each November in the heart of Regent Park in t’karonto, the festival is proud to welcome new theatrical, dance, music, and multidisciplinary works reflecting the breadth of Indigenous experiences, the richness of Indigenous arts, and offering a peek into Indigenous storytelling today and to come. 
 
Factory season artwork by Mark Krzepis krzepism

What You Won’t Do For Love, starring Drs. David Suzuki and Tara Cullis, will be presented by Factory on the mainstage (October 21 – 22, 2026). This Why Not Theatre Production will be presented as part of an 8 city North Amercian tour! 

After 50 years of marriage and a lifetime devoted to climate activism, environmental icons David Suzuki and Tara Cullis take to the stage with a rare behind-the-scenes look at a life shaped by deep love, a commitment to joy, and the courage to act. 

Photo of David and Tara by Dahlia Katz.

As a part of RUTAS 2026, Factory is co-presenting the Spanish language premiere of Mujer Venado | Deer Woman (October 1 – 3, 2026), produced by ARTICLE 11 with Aluna Theatre. 

Lila is a warrior. She is the daughter of a hunter who taught her all he knew. She’s ex-army, too. When circumstances converge, Lila finds the perfect opportunity to avenge her baby sister’s murder while exercising the skills taught by the Canadian government. Written by Tara Beagan. 

Season artwork by Mark Krzepis krzepism

Illustration of Lissete VC.

We’re kicking off the season (in a couple days!) with the return of the SummerWorks Performance Festival (August 6 - 16, 2026). 

Be sure to catch festival programming Provisions (Lester Trips (Theatre)), Soft Squishy Things (Ghost River Theatre / Macromatter), and the prolific SummerWorks closing party at Factory. 

This year’s Festival theme, Fight | Flight brings forward urgent creative responses to this troubling moment in time. Across the 2026 Festival, artists root themselves in place, in community, in ancestry, and in practice, while also shifting perspectives, rewriting histories, and creating new narratives through the body, exploring memory, consent, transformation, and identity, through resistance, humour, and intimacy. 

Factory season artwork by Mark Krzepis krzepism

The wait is over: we’re over the moon to share our fall 2026 programming! 

Fall 2026 at Factory is an eclectic mix of festivals, thought provoking stage productions, and fun favourites from long time friends and brand new collaborators. Check out our website to discover the lineup, we can’t wait to welcome you 💓

Sophie, Meilie and Wai Yin, three Chinese women, come together to watch a video adaptation Sophie made of the classic play The Maids (Les Bonnes) by Jean Genet. Together as they watch the video – where two Chinese women play the maids and fantasize their revenge on their Madame – the friends speak candidly about their childhood, their love-hate relationship with whiteness, the colonization of their minds, and Crazy Rich Asians. They discuss their evolving feelings about their Chinese identity; from shame to pride to deep concern, especially in a world where China’s financial and political power continues to grow. And why do an adaptation of a play by a dead white guy anyway? Differences amongst the women emerge and tensions grow until Sophie’s desire for revenge on whiteness boils over.  
Bonnes Bonnes combines documentary theatre, live on-stage cooking, projections and movement to explore how we can heal from the wounds of internalized racism.

Announcing the facilitator of the 2026 TEPs acting stream, Khadijah Roberts-Abdullah!

Khadijah Roberts-Abdullah is a Toronto based actor, writer, and director. Living her life at a multitude of intersections, Khadijah’s work is motivated by a pursuit of artistic expression that aims to challenge understandings of visibility and inclusivity. Whether working alongside like-minded artists or producing work through her company, 2Skins Entertainment, Khadijah strives to create art that amplifies the voices of those who exist in the margins of our society. Her multimedia production company has created a Black femme horror review podcast titled Ghoulz n Gyaldem.  She co-wrote and starred in her first short film, P!GS, in 2018 and followed it up with her second short, DEFUND, which premiered at TIFF 2021. DEFUND was also named one of TIFF’s Top Ten Canadian Short Films and is available for streaming as a Vimeo Staff Pick. Notable acting credits include; Slo-Pitch (Crave/Shaftesbury/Boss & Co), The Last of Us (HBO), American Gods (Freemantle/Starz), What We Do In The Shadows (FX), Workin Moms (CBC), and three seasons in the Stratford Festival.

Introducing our September STACKTˣ Winner: callthepapaurazzi 💖

Some things are felt, others are seen. Call the Papaurazzi lives somewhere in between, capturing the energy you bring into a room and turning it into colour through aura photography, biofeedback technology, and film.

Rooted in spirituality with a Y2K state of mind, their portraits are less about posing for the camera and more about capturing a moment in time. The moods, shifts, and shades that make you, you.
Because no colour is good or bad. Just like emotions, they come, they go, they change — and we think that’s kind of dope.✨

Here for a good time, not a long time. Catch them @ STACKT marketplace until October 4 in Unit 5-108.

🚗🚆 GETTING TO HENDERSON DURING RUSH WEEK(S) 🚆🚗

With Rush back home and the neighbourhood about to get very busy, here are the easiest ways to get to Henderson this week and next:

🚗 DRIVING & PAID PARKING
We will have limited parking available on-site.

⭐ YOUR BEST PARKING OPTION ⭐
The Hines Parking Garage is located at 152 Sterling Road—just west of MOCA and a short walk from Henderson. Hourly and daily paid parking is available.

Street parking around Sterling Road is extremely limited and subject to strict time and permit restrictions, so we strongly recommend using the Hines Garage.

🚆 UP EXPRESS
Coming from Union Station or Pearson Airport? Take the UP Express to Bloor Station. From there, it’s a short walk to the brewery.

🚇 SUBWAY
Dundas West and Lansdowne stations are both on Line 2 and approximately a 10-to-15-minute walk from Henderson.

🚋 STREETCAR
Take the 506 Carlton to Dundas Street West at Sterling Road. We’re just a three-minute walk down Sterling.

🚌 BUS
Take the 47 Lansdowne bus to Lansdowne Avenue at Bloor Street West. Henderson is approximately a 10-minute walk away.

🚕 UBER/LYFT
Enter Henderson Brewing Company—128A Sterling Road—as your destination.

Plan ahead. Get here safely. Grab a Rush beer. 🍻

dropinthebucket.name: Drop in The Bucket
dropinthebucket.biography: We build wells & sanitation systems at schools throughout sub-Saharan Africa, enabling youth to fully harness the life-changing power of an education.

media.caption:
What Happens When You Stop Traffic for a Day and Let the Girls Take Over?

Every October in Nimule, South Sudan, police stop traffic on one of the country's busiest roads so schoolgirls can march through town celebrating International Day of the Girl.

It's a joyful day of singing, dancing and speeches. But in a country where girls face enormous barriers to education, there's a much bigger reason to celebrate... 

Check out the latest blog post on our website about yesterday's event (Link in bio)

#southsudan #dropinthebucket #cleanwaterandeducationforall

At the end of the regular school day in Nimule, more than 1500 girls don’t necessarily go straight home. Many stay for another couple of hours and go to one of our Safe Spaces.

Safe Spaces are after-school programs for girls in 5th through 8th grade, the years when we have seen many girls begin to leave school. Some are struggling academically. Some families can no longer manage school costs. Girls may be under pressure to marry early or needed at home to help with domestic work. There isn’t one reason girls drop out, which means there isn’t one solution for keeping them there.

The girls come to Safe Spaces for extra help in Math and English, but that’s only part of what happens there. To read more check out the blog on our website (Link in bio)

Becoming a mother doesn't have to mean the end of an education. Our Safe Spaces for Young Mothers in South Sudan program provides mentoring, tutoring, counseling, life skills training, and practical support that helps young mothers return to school, complete their education, and create brighter futures for themselves and their children. #safespaces #safespacesforyoungmothers #southsudan #dropinthebucket #educationisahumanright

Just a reminder that people, especially children are the most important thing and despite what you may see on the news, Uganda is a country filled with bright smiles and happy kids excited about the future.

Drop in the Bucket did not drill this well! 

So why are we posting photos of a well we didn't drill?

Not every area needs a  brand new well, some just need the well they have repaired, 
We are currently rehabilitating some wells originally drilled by other organizations. These are organizations are no longer operating in the region — in doing this we are restoring clean water access for schools and communities that would otherwise be left behind.

A repaired well can mean children spend less time walking for water, families avoid unsafe water sources, and entire communities regain something essential.
This well is flowing again. And so is the future around it.

#CleanWater #Uganda #WaterForAfrica #WaterCharity #Nonprofit #Africa #CleanWaterForAll
Clean water for Angal village in Gulu District in Uganda. #drilledbydrop #dropinthebucket #uganda #gulu #africawaterwells

This well was completed last year at a village called Amacat, near Gulu, Uganda. I couldn't help but smile when I noticed the curious, but nervous young boy watching on and just managing to end up in two of the three photos. Eventually he got braver and now we are all friends. #dropinthebucket #uganda #gulu #cleanwater

Team building in Nimule, South Sudan. After the successful 2025 Inter-school Quiz Game event, the South Sudan DROP team took a minute for a team building celebration. 2026 will be anothr busy but productive year and we are ready to face any challenges that come our way. #dropinthebucket #southsudan #waterandeducation

Happy Thanksgiving from all of us. As we look back on a busy year of growth and challenges, we’re grateful to do this work—because of you.

Thank you for making it possible.
“When water is near, life is near.” — African proverb #cleanwater #dropinthebucket #bepartofthesolution #uganda

In Paminano-A village in Uganda, water once moved like currency—lent, borrowed, even “repaid with interest.”
Okello Martin and the water committee now steward a new borehole, turning scarcity into shared access and routine. To read more about this unusual situation, visit our website (link in bio) #cleanwater #waterandsanitation #bepartofthesolution #dropinthebucket
On a day that holds so many emotions for so many, we reflect on how kindness always makes a difference.
Clean water is the first step towards a brighter future for this girl and her entire village. #uganda #cleanwater #watercharity #bepartofthesolution #dropinthebucket

Education does not have to end with motherhood. In Nimule, our Safe Spaces give adolescent mothers a second chance at going back to school.

Each afternoon, groups of young mothers gather to study literacy and numeracy, share parenting tips, and lean on mentors who understand the road back to school. Child-care is on-site, so a crying baby never means missing a lesson.

The goal is simple: help every girl who wants to return to formal schooling cross that threshold with confidence and the support she deserves.

Because when a mother finishes school, her child grows up seeing a world of better options.

#SafeSpaces #GirlsEducation #BackToSchool #SouthSudan #DropInTheBucket

Clean water changed this girl's life - help us help more children in Uganda. Go to our website to see how you can get involved. www.dropinthebucket.org or see link in bio.

#cleanwater #dropinthebucket #waterchangeseverything

In Labworomor village, Nwoya, Uganda, this mother now collects clean water without walking for miles.

With a child in front and a baby on her back, she’s doing what mothers do best — carrying the future forward.

This well, drilled by Drop in the Bucket, is changing daily life in Labworomor.

#WaterForAfrica #UgandaWaterWell #AfricaWaterCharity #CleanWaterChangesEverything #Nwoya #DropInTheBucket

This Mother’s Day, Celebrate the Strength of Mothers Everywhere

Some mothers skip meals so their children can eat. Others go without sleep, rest, or comfort—always putting their children first.

And some mothers walk miles each day just to collect water for their families.
Every day, we meet incredible women whose love, sacrifice, and determination ensure their children have a chance at a better life. Clean water and education open up a world of possibilities for children.

Because of you, more mothers can raise healthy children with clean water nearby—and send them to school with hope for the future.

This Mother’s Day, give water. Give education. Give opportunity.

#cleanwaterandeducationforall #dropinthebucket #cleanwater #watercharity

In Aleng C village, Uganda, Auno Kevin’s family relied on a hand-dug waterhole that filled with mud every time it rained. A new borehole changed everything.

See last slide for a photo of Auno Kevin and read her full story on our website dropinthebucket.org (link in bio)

Before the Well

This was the only water source for the people of Pudyek Cell.

Families collected water from the same muddy hole that animals drank from. The only alternative? A privately owned borehole that led to tensions as people “borrowed” water day and night.

Clean water shouldn’t be a privilege. It should be a right.

Swipe to see what happened next.

#CleanWaterForAll #WaterCrisis #UgandaWaterWell

Meet the children of Pabidi! This village in the Amuru, District of northern Uganda just got clean water for the first time. Before this well, the only option was collecting water from unreliable sources. Now? Safe, clean water is just a few steps away. 

##CleanWaterForAll #waterandeducationforall #cleanwater #waterforafrica #changingliveswithwater

What a difference clean water makes! 

Imagine waking up every morning knowing your only water source looks like the image in the first photo. Now imagine the relief of finally having access to the well in the second photo. 

This is what World Water Day is about—real change, real impact. Every well we drill means families no longer have to drink unsafe water or spend hours walking to fetch it.

Water changes everything. Join us in making it accessible for more communities. Go to our website www.dropinthebucket.org and see how on this World Water Day - you can make a difference. (link in bio)

#worldwaterday #cleanwaterforall #waterchangeseverything #dropinthebucket

New post on the DROP website for International Women's Day 2025. 

The world today can feel overwhelming, with challenges that look different from place to place. While circumstances may vary, uncertainty and obstacles affect us all. In many parts of the world, women are still fighting for opportunities that others may take for granted—whether it’s access to education, a voice in their community, or a safe place to give birth. At times, progress may seem fragile, but we cannot afford to lose hope—because now, more than ever, the world needs us to keep moving forward.

At Drop in the Bucket, we see that empowering women transforms entire communities. That’s why we are committed to expanding educational opportunities for girls in South Sudan—one of the most challenging places in the world for female education. This year alone, over 250 girls are enrolled in our scholarship program, giving them the chance to stay in school and build brighter futures.

Use the link below to read the rest of this post.

https://dropinthebucket.org/2025/03/10/international-womens-day/

Drop in the Bucket currently runs five safe spaces in the Nimule district—dedicated after-school centers where primary-age girls can participate in activities, receive extra coaching, and feel empowered in a safe, supportive environment.

#waterandeducationforall #southsudan #nimule #safespaces

World Toilet Day: A new standard for sanitation in Gulu, Uganda 

Safe sanitation is a human right, and at Kasubi Central Primary School in Gulu, Uganda, we’ve turned that right into a reality. 🚽✨

With the help of Drop in the Bucket:
💧 Flushing toilets
♻️ An eco-friendly septic system 
🙌 A water-saving system powered by a handpump and a unique roundabout pump

These upgrades mean healthier students, better hygiene, and brighter futures for 548 children. 🌟

Together, we can bring safe sanitation to even more communities. Join us today. Link in bio!

#WorldToiletDay #SanitationMatters #CleanWater #WASH #EducationForAll

"Because no matter who we are or where we come from, we're all entitled to the basic human rights of clean air to breathe, clean water to drink, and healthy land to call home." -Martin Luther King III #waterislife #watercharity #dropinthebucket #uganda

Last week, we celebrated International Day of the Girl Child, honoring the incredible strength and achievements of girls in our education program in Nimule, South Sudan, and girls around the world. 🌍✨

Though we held off on posting due to the devastation caused by Hurricane Milton, we still want to recognize these girls who continue to achieve greatness despite the odds. Their resilience is truly inspiring.

A big thank you to our friends at jblaudio jbl_pro for donating the PA system that made our celebration unforgettable! 

#InternationalDayoftheGirl #IDG2024 #DropInTheBucket #EducationForAll #Nimule #JBL

Today, on the International Day of Peace, we celebrate the strength, resilience, and unwavering hope of the people of South Sudan. Though challenges remain, the strides taken toward peace show the world the power of unity and community in the face of adversity.

From grassroots initiatives to national efforts, South Sudanese men, women, and youth are working together to rebuild a future where peace, education, and opportunity thrive. It’s a reminder that peace is not just an end goal but a daily commitment to kindness, dialogue, and collaboration.

At Drop in the Bucket, we believe that access to clean water and education is a cornerstone of lasting peace. When communities have these essential resources, they can focus on building a brighter future for their children, free from the fears of conflict and instability.

Let us stand with South Sudan and the world in celebrating peace, and continue working towards a day when every child grows up in a world filled with opportunity and hope.

#InternationalDayOfPeace #SouthSudan #HopeForPeace #DropInTheBucket #PeaceAndWater #StrongerTogether

Need a reason to smile today? The Kasubi Central Primary School in Uganda is filled with happy smiling faces right now. After years of struggling with poor sanitation, the school finally has toilets thanks to one incredible family who visited the school with us last year and asked if they could fund a toilet. 

We were happy to oblige and now the school has one of our flushing eco-sustainable sanitation systems. The system does not require any power and the unique design ensures that it never fills up or needs to be emptied. 

As you can see from the smiling faces in the photos the children are thrilled.

Jake Vaadeland (jake_vaadeland)is a self taught multi-instrumentalist and songwriter from Saskatchewan. His traditional sound and unique style could be defined as a blend of bluegrass and 50s rockabilly. Jake strives to write and play with a focus on storytelling and messages that he hopes his audience can relate to, all packaged in foot stomping, high energy performances with The Sturgeon River Boys.

In 2022, Jake received 2 Saskatchewan Music Awards, including Album of the Year for his album Everybody But Me, along with Roots/Folk Artist of the Year. He followed that up in 2023 by once again winning the Roots/Folk Artist of the Year. He was awarded four 2022 Saskatchewan Country Music Awards, including Fans Choice Entertainer of the Year, Songwriter of the Year, Alternative Album of the Year & Emerging Artist of the Year, and again followed up in 2023 by winning the Alternative Album award for the 2nd year in row. Jake was also nominated for Roots/Folk Artist of the Year at the 2023 Western Canadian Music Awards.

Jake had another big year at the 2024 Saskatchewan Country Music Awards, taking home 4 awards including Male Artist of the Year, Songwriter of the Year, Video of the Year & Interactive Artist of the Year. He was also nominated for Best New Touring Artist at the Canadian Live Music Industry Awards and is nominated once again for Roots/Folk Artist of the Year at the Western Canadian Music Awards.

His new album, Retro Man…More And More (Expanded Edition) was released in April, 2024, This was followed up in May, 2024 when Jake joined Platinum selling Canadian country artist, Tebey for the release of their single, Wake Me Up (the Bluegrass Rendition). These releases are being supported by extensive tours in Canada, USA, UK and EU. Jake Vaadeland & the Sturgeon River Boys have developed a reputation as one of the hardest working independent bands in the business. True road warriors, they are passionate about taking their music directly to their quickly growing fanbase around the world.

Sam Jr.'s sophomore album, Inner Shadow, was released on May 31, 2024 via Arts & Crafts (Echodelick Records in the USA, Weird Beard in the UK and Worst Bassist Records in the EU). Dark, edgy, and contemplative, this album intersperses his signature fuzzy, industrial rock tones with his melancholic musings on modern living.

New to Sam Jr.? Check out his 2022 debut album's nihilist fuzz-psychedelic haze. It's your hot new fuzz. The hot new fuzz. But judge for yourself. If you're into hot fuzz, Sam Jr.'s debut album will make you rather happy.

"My concept for awhile writing songs was actually, 'What would the Dude’s band from The Big Lebowski sound like?'" laughs Sam Jr., the titular architect behind this long-overdue solo stepping-out. "I'm not sure it landed there at all, but I'm trying to harness the easygoing nature and spirit of that character."

If you enjoy overdriven Stooges sleaze and expertly deployed noise of the Spacemen 3 / A Place to Bury Strangers variety, and the thought of, say, T. Rex covering some of the more obscure B-sides on Barbed Wire Kisses or the Primal Scream who made XTRMNTR going back in time to remake Screamadelica with far more cynicism ... well, that's in the ballpark. But why give it all away? If it sounds like you're gonna like it, you're probably gonna love it.

GENERAL MOJO'S (generalmojos) are a psychedelic rock band from Seattle, WA, with over a decade of history in the Northwest, but creating a contemporary sound daily. Composed of four generational talents, Unleashed Entertainment has described them as “the band with no weak link.” The ensemble found their PNW voice within the richly established DIY scene, performing primarily in house shows. While a shimmering psych-pop presence in the music has cemented itself, the band has widened their influences and performances, playing electric shows festivals across the Northwest USA and internationally. In 2024, band members were featured in the score and music of Orlando Bloom film Red Right Hand.

-

DANNY WEBSTER (danny_webster_) is a singer-songwriter and multi-instrumentalist based out of Toronto. Raised in a small town in Ontario, Danny was raised on his mother’s love of classical music and his father’s of 80s metal, becoming fascinated by music from a young age.  His lyrics tend to focus on loss, love, grief, fear, and anxiety, listing his main influences as Big Thief, Tame Impala, ABBA, Bon Iver, Radiohead and Alex G. Aged 24 now, he intendsto continue exploring different genres in his writing and continues to perform with his backing band.

-

JUSTIN OROK (justin.orok) is a Toronto-based singer songwriter and guitarist, best known for his unique narrative songwriting and sensitive approach on both steel string and lap steel guitar. His debut album, Kanata, was released in 2022, independently in Canada and under the short-lived Paraphenalia Records in Japan.  It features many Canadian jazz, improvised and folk mainstays including Justin Haynes, Felicity Williams, Christine Bougie, Andrew Downing, Michael Davidson, Jesse Zubot and was produced by Jean Martin (Barnyard Records, Tanya Tagaq).

 In the Summer of 2003 the power went out. It left over 50 million people without electricity across most of Ontario and eight U.S. states.

While this kind of thing is a common occurrence in most of the rest of the world, we take this as a yearly reminder to celebrate the community that took care of one another during that time, by taking over the streets for a picnic and parade. Please bring your bike and come dance and frolic and stare in amazement at the hugeness of our collective power, remembering a time we were literally powerless 💡🚲🕯️

THIS ONE IS FOR THE YEARNERS ❤️‍🔥❤️‍🔥‼️🗣️🤭 Our next Listening Room honours the iconic R&B catalog of 13x Grammy winner, Babyface!! 

From his classic 80s bops to his lustful R&B ballads, Babyface’s pen runs deep through the world of R&B music and beyond. For these jam sessions we’ll be sonically exploring his massive catalogue of not just his own music, but the songs he produced and song wrote for🪩💿😆 Y’all NEED to bring out your mamas and aunties for some nostalgic joy! The room will be filled with magic as we jam to and transform these songs that we all love so much! 

WE ARE NOW ON DICE - BAND ANNOUNCEMENT AND OFFICIAL TICKET SALE BEGINS Thursday October 15, @ 12PM 👀🎫

—

Listening Room is a jam series inspired by the Soulquarians process of music creation in which we will listen to the music of Babyface, our houseband will demonstrate how they creatively re-imagine the music (as if Babyface called them into his studio), and thirdly, our stage will open up to more exceptional Toronto musicians to participate in the musical magic making 🪄🎶 

Musicians band music lovers alike are invited to step into this intimate space to listen, vibe, and jam!

GET YOUR TICKETS ON DICE ON THURSDAY OCTOBER 15 @ 12PM🚨

*please note that Listening Room is a jam series featuring Toronto-based musicians and Babyface is not scheduled to perform at these jams.

*tickets are non-transferable

“Is it too late for me to start dancing?”
“I have two left feet”
“I can’t remember the steps”
“Improvisation sounds scary”

If any of these thoughts sound familiar, you’re not alone.

You don’t need a dance background, perfect flexibility, or all the answers before your first class. There’s room to feel, ask questions, and find your own way of moving.

Swipe through for a few worries you might recognise🌿

Curious about joining us in Waterloo or Richmond Hill? Send me a message. I’d love to hear from you.

Science PhDs dancing their research thesis? Don’t miss this!

Dance Your PhD is a competition since 2008 run by Science and AAAS. The idea is pretty simple:
Take your PhD research. 
Turn it into a dance video. 
And put it on YouTube.

I watched a lot of the videos — from photons, to zebrafish, to river restoration and yeast cells…

What I love most is seeing people of different backgrounds bring their own knowledge, curiosity and experience into movement and dance work!

Sources and credits of all dance films are noted in the video.

Curious about contemporary dance, but not sure where to start?

This beginner-friendly class is for adults who want to move, explore and enjoy dancing — no previous dance experience needed.

In class, we explore the fundamentals of contemporary dance through weight, flow, momentum and coordination, with guided improvisation and short choreographic phrases. We take things step by step, so you can move at your own pace while gradually building confidence and movement skills.

💃A beginner-friendly class for adults who want to move, explore and enjoy dancing — no previous dance experience needed. 

🍀Each class combines:

MOVEMENT
Explore the fundamentals of contemporary dance through weight, flow, momentum, coordination and different movement qualities.

IMPROVISATION
Follow simple guided prompts to move more freely, get curious about your body, and discover new movement possibilities.

CHOREOGRAPHY
Learn contemporary dance phrases and experience how movements connect, travel and flow together. We usually learn one piece of choreography over a four-class cycle, building it up gradually from week to week.

What exactly is contemporary dance?

I’ve realised this is surprisingly difficult to answer — because contemporary dance is probably defined as much by the questions it keeps asking as by any particular movement style.

So here’s my three-minute attempt: from Isadora Duncan and modern dance, to postmodernism, and to the wonderfully hard-to-define field we have today.

For me, contemporary dance is less about rebellion than openness and curiosity — being open to different bodies, aesthetics and perspectives, while staying curious about what dance can be, why we dance, and how we might move.

This is how I understand it at this moment. I’m sure that understanding will keep changing too.

This is the Beefcake Manifesto!

If you don't know me as a person, this manifesto will give you a little more of an idea of my personal goals and ethics behind Beefcake Strength Training!
I've become the trainer I wish I had coming into my own fitness journey. 

Working with me, will be:

Body positive: Our bodies can do so many things. And so many of those things have nothing to do with size or thinness. I love celebrating all that our bodies do while we move heavy shit around!

Personalized: Everyone comes to me with different goals, access to equipment, and availability. I work as hard as I can to incorporate all of these factors into a workout program that works for you!

Caring: I seriously love what I do. I love heavy things, I care about my community, and I love watching people's limiting ideas of what they think is possible for their bodies get absolutely shattered. I want to make this journey as supportive as possible. 

Fun: You will sweat, you will curse me, you will complain, but it's all worth it for my jokes!!

Challenging: This is the whole point! Without challenge, there is no change or growth. I'll guide you, while always pushing you to do more than you thought was possible!

Educational: my favourite!! There's so much in fitness that is gatekept, and I'm not about that. If there's anything you want to know about strength and fitness, I will talk your ear off about it, or find the relevant information. My aim is to share my knowledge with people! 

DM me or email beefcakecontact@gmail.com if these goals speak to you and you want to start working together!

Hey, it's me!
I'm Nadine, a Tkaronto-based personal trainer! I've been a fitness and movement enthusiast for most of my life, and I want to bring that enthusiasm to my community. 
My aim is to make strength both fun and approachable! So reach out if you're interested in lifting logs and shit!

That's right! I'm taking new clients! Whether you want someone to fine tune your exercise program, teach you what all those cables and machines at the gym do, or motivate and encourage you weekly, I'm the one for you! Reach out, and let's get sweaty!

A little bit more to the intro from the previous post! As you begin to explore this community, it’s important for me that you know and understand the ethos behind my class: move your body in a way that feels good for you! ✨

It’s not about getting every step or doing exactly what I’m doing. It’s not about perfecting dance steps or choreography. It’s about feeling and connecting to the music with your body. It also means understanding and regularly checking in with yourself - some days we can give high energy and intensity and other times we may need to keep to softer movements, and that’s absolutely okay! Trust your body to move and enjoy the way that music can inspire you to explore movement and keep moving! 💃🙏🏽

And on that note, another personal moment to share how Zumba further introduced me to Latin music and has since propelled my love for learning salsa and bachata (for which I do separate training and classes). 

What’s your movement story? Please share below, I’d love to know! ⬇️

Amy Sedaris, from The Second City Mainstage to cult-comedy legend💫

Sedaris was cutting her teeth at The Second City in the late ’80s—quickly rising through the Touring Company, then to Second City Northwest in Rolling Meadows, and eventually onto the Mainstage, where she performed alongside Stephen Colbert, Steve Carell, and Paul Dinello.

At the same time, she was co-writing plays with her brother, David Sedaris—earning them the nickname “The Talent Family.”

Next stop: New York.

She co-created Exit 57 for Comedy Central with Dinello, alongside fellow Second City alums including Paul Dinello, Mitch Rouse, and Stephen Colbert. Then came cult classic Strangers with Candy (and its 2006 film adaptation), cementing Sedaris as one of comedy’s most original voices.

She’s since voiced Princess Carolyn on BoJack Horseman, hosted the delightfully unhinged At Home with Amy Sedaris, appeared in Dolly Parton’s “Better Get to Livin’” video, and authored books including I Like You: Entertaining Under the Influence and Simple Times: Crafts for Poor People.

Always a delightfully original comedic voice ♥️

Did you know Martin Short originally stepped onto The Second City Toronto stage in 1977, taking over for John Candy?

He replaced him in their ninth revue, “The Wizard of Ossington.” This was before they both rose to fame on SCTV. (Check out iconic photo #2)

Martin originally brought his character “Ed Grimley” to Second City Television (SCTV) and later to Saturday Night Live.

From there came comedy classics like Three Amigos! and roles like Franck the wedding planner in Father of the Bride, and of course, the incomparable Jiminy Glick.

Short was recently the subject of the documentary Marty: Life Is Short, which celebrates his extraordinary ability to find humor and connection even in the face of profound loss and grief. We’re grateful for his unparalleled ability to spread joy in the world, both on stage and off.

“I would not say that my work at Second City had intellectual appeal as much as more of a clown quality.” — Martin Short

Let us tell you about a woman named Mina Kolb.
Mina was part of the original cast of the very first Second City revue in 1959. Today, she turns 100 years old.

In honor of this milestone, we are officially declaring today Mina Kolb Day at The Second City (and, frankly, everywhere else).

She joined the inaugural Second City company alongside co-founder Howard Alk, Roger Bowen, Severn Darden, Andrew Duncan, Barbara Harris, Eugene Troobnick, and pianist William Allaudin Mathieu. Kolb was already a familiar face in Chicago. She and local television icon Ray Rayner had spent five years on the popular program Rayner Shine, where they lip-synced to records while teenagers danced on set. 

Remarkably, Kolb had never improvised before joining The Second City.

In 1961, she moved to Los Angeles to appear on the CBS sitcom Pete and Gladys, launching a career that would span decades. Her credits also include Three’s Company, Christopher Guest’s A Mighty Wind, Jeff Garlin’s I Want Someone to Eat Cheese With, Curb Your Enthusiasm, and more.

Join us in wishing a very happy 100th birthday to Second City pioneer, Mina Kolb ❤️

Jack McBrayer was recently on armchairexppod and reminisced about The Second City. Thought we’d shared some photos from his time here!

McBrayer saw his first Second City show in 1995, which inspired him to start taking classes. Eventually he’d become part of the touring company, and the e.t.c stage. McBrayer’s southern charm, Georgia accent, and character work made him a crowd favorite at The Second City where he worked alongside castmates like Keegan-Michael Key and T.J. Jagodowski.

It was during this time period that he met Tina Fey through her husband Jeff Richmond. From there, he was eventually hand-picked to play the role of “Kenneth,” the NBC Page on Tina Fey’s 30 Rock. The role (written with McBrayer in mind) provided McBrayer with an opportunity to play to his strong suits and create a truly memorable character in a character-driven show.

McBrayer had unforgettable appearances on Late Night with Conan O’Brien, Drunk History, Talladega Nights: The Ballad of Ricky Bobby, Walk Hard: The Dewey Cox Story, Forgetting Sarah Marshall, Bob’s Burgers and The Simpsons, among so many others.

His interview on Armchair Expert is definitely worth a listen, and is linked in our bio!

As colbert signs off from late night, looking back at some moments from the time he spent at The Second City.

Colbert started at The Second City working the box office in 1987. He’d answer phones by day, take classes by night, and actually held a longtime record for most t-shirts sold in a single day.

Comedy wasn’t originally the plan, but dabbling in the improv scene changed everything. Colbert sharpened a voice that would help redefine political satire for a generation, collaborating alongside future comedy icons like Amy Sedaris, Paul Dinello, and Steve Carell along the way.

Through every stage of his career, he carried the intelligence, humanity, and fearless point of view that stood out from the very beginning.

From selling t-shirts to helping to shape late night television. Not a bad career pivot.

We wish Mr. Colbert the best of luck on his future endeavors!

Improv Supernova goes back to the basics…improv as a form of connection.

Every single show is built around the specific audience in that room that night—shaped through ongoing conversation, shared energy, and the willingness to play together.

What starts as a suggestion becomes something bigger: a moment everyone helped create together, alongside a room full of strangers who won’t feel like strangers for long. It’s what live theater is meant to be.

Tickets and showtimes at the link in bio 🎟️

Improv isn’t just about getting laughs—it’s about becoming a better person.

You learn how to truly listen, respond in the moment, and build on someone else’s idea instead of shutting it down. That “yes, and” mindset? It doesn’t stay on stage—it shows up in your conversations, your relationships, and your day-to-day life.

You start to read the room faster. Communicate more clearly. Trust your instincts. Let go of overthinking. And maybe most importantly, you get comfortable being yourself around other people. 

Somewhere between the games, the scenes, and the unexpected moments, you build real confidence and real connection.

The next term of the Training Center starts soon! Link in bio for more info.

It was on The Second City stage where Chris Farley first introduced the now-iconic motivational speaker Matt Foley, a character that would later become a cultural phenomenon on SNL. Lorne Michaels saw Farley perform and brought him to New York in 1990.

The rest is comedy history.

Raised in Wisconsin, Farley started practicing improv in Madison and eventually made his way to Chicago to study improv under the legendary Del Close. He started in The Second City Touring Company, and joined the Mainstage in 1989, performing alongside future comedy powerhouses like Tim Meadows, Bob Odenkirk, Joel Murray, and David Pasquesi.

No matter how big his career became, Farley never forgot his roots. He often returned to The Second City stage to jump into improv sets with the next generation of comedians, even attending the company’s holiday party just days before his passing in 1997.

He’ll always have a place in the hearts of the people who worked with him or saw him perform ❤️

Today, we’re sharing the bittersweet news that, after almost five years of dedicated leadership, Gideon Arthurs will step down as Executive Director of Soulpepper Theatre on October 30.

Gideon joined Soulpepper in 2022 as we prepared to reopen following the pandemic. During his tenure, we welcomed artists and audiences back, expanded our role beyond the stage through ambitious civic and community programming, and welcomed Paolo Santalucia as Artistic Director.

Much of an Executive Director’s work happens behind the scenes, but if you’ve joined us for a show, concert, free film, public conversation or community gathering over the past four years, you’ve experienced the impact of Gideon’s leadership.

As Paolo’s inaugural season gets underway, Soulpepper enters its next chapter with renewed momentum, a growing community and an exciting year of theatre, music and civic programming ahead.

Please join us in celebrating Gideon’s remarkable contribution to Soulpepper and wishing him all the very best for what comes next. ❤️

A RECORD-BREAKING NIGHT
 
Last evening, Crow’s hosted our 9th Annual Financial Services Evening (FSE), welcoming peers from across the financial and professional services sector for a memorable evening of connection, and live theatre.
 
Guests took over Crow’s for a vibrant night of food, cocktails, and conversation, culminating in a special performance of A FINE BALANCE, Anosh Irani's remarkable stage adaptation of Rohinton Mistry's beloved novel.
 
It was a particularly meaningful work to share with this community. At its heart, A FINE BALANCE is a story about resilience, compassion, and the unexpected connections that sustain us through life's most difficult circumstances. We were deeply moved by the conversations it inspired among our guests, a reminder of theatre's extraordinary ability to bring people together, challenge our perspectives, and deepen our understanding of one another.
 
And together, we achieved something remarkable: FSE 2026 raised more than $300,000, a new fundraising record for this signature event!
 
This generosity directly supports the work on our stages: investing in artists, developing new Canadian theatre, and making it possible for Crow’s to continue bringing bold, ambitious productions to life.

Our heartfelt thanks to FSE Chair Hung Ko and committee members Anne Maggisano and Lawrence Lewis, whose leadership, advocacy, and dedication have been instrumental in making this evening such a success.
 
To our 2026 sponsors: thank you for your generosity, partnership, and commitment to Crow’s Theatre.

The company of MACBETH gathered for the first day of rehearsals yesterday, ahead of the anticipated production's debut. The visionary creative team behind this solo performance is transforming the haunting tragedy to be set against the cutthroat world of the modern tech industry.

One prophecy sets the scene for Macbeth’s terrifying unraveling, where every thought, every fear, every choice pushes him beyond the point of no return. In this electrifying reimagining, the collision of unstoppable technology and human free will forces us to confront the fragility – and ferocity – of the human spirit.

Discover what happens when the scale of a Shakespearean tragedy is transformed into a gripping ninety-minute performance.

The company of MEASURE FOR MEASURE reunited this week for their first rehearsal, ahead of the acclaimed production’s return. It’s like no time has passed since House + Body’s Shakespeare reimagining filled the theatre and the cast and crew’s chemistry was clear from the first day back together.

When Isabella’s brother is sentenced to death, she embarks on a journey to save his life but is forced to confront a system where authority wavers and moral certainty erodes. Watch as five actors juggle twenty roles live on air, racing through a high-stakes broadcast as offstage antics spiral as wildly as the drama that unfolds.

Tickets on sale NOW for ALL’S WELL.
 
The wait is almost over for ALL’S WELL, the celebrated national bestseller by Mona Awad, adapted for the stage in a darkly funny, deliciously wicked World Premiere this November.
 
Revenge, fantasy and reinvention collide in a razor-sharp comedy about ambition, pain and power, where getting exactly what you want can come with wicked fine print.
 
Starring Maev Beaty (Ransacking Troy, Secret Life of a Mother), adapted for the stage by Governor General’s Award-winner Erin Shields (Ransacking Troy, Paradise Lost), and directed by Jackie Maxwell, former Artistic Director of the Shaw Festival.
 
From the bestselling author of BUNNY, ROUGE and WE LOVE YOU, BUNNY.
